By forming transient SNARE assemblies in neuronal cell bodies and apical dendrites, it promotes membrane merger during vesicle transport and cargo delivery.

A multi-pass endoplasmic reticulum membrane enzyme that installs ethanolamine phosphate onto glycosylphosphatidylinositol intermediates during anchor assembly. Its N-terminal alkaline-phosphatase-like catalytic core performs metal-dependent phosphotransfer, while a large C-terminal membrane region anchors and positions the active site within the ER bilayer. By transferring ethanolamine phosphate to the nascent GPI scaffold, it drives a key step in GPI-anchor biosynthesis that ultimately tethers many surface proteins.

A mitochondrial SAM-dependent methyltransferase that catalyzes a ring-methyl transfer step in coenzyme Q biosynthesis. It operates as a soluble, matrix-exposed enzyme that associates with the inner membrane and assembles into a biosynthetic complex to methylate a quinone-ring intermediate, thereby advancing coenzyme Q production and sustaining mitochondrial energy metabolism. Its fold and conserved catalytic site coordinate methyl-group transfer, while multivalent contacts stabilize pathway assemblies at the membrane–matrix interface.

A secreted venom peptide from a scorpion that adopts a disulfide-stabilized knottin fold to act as a potent extracellular toxin. Its rigid CS-alpha/beta scaffold presents pharmacophore loops that bind and modulate membrane ion channels on other organisms, thereby disrupting excitability and causing immobilization or death. By incapacitating prey or adversaries through extracellular targeting and high structural stability, it contributes to defense and predation in the extracellular environment.

A large, soluble scaffold that assembles tandem beta-propeller modules to organize spindle-associated protein complexes in mouse cells. By leveraging extensive WD-repeat architecture and an EML-like core, it binds multiple partners to stabilize and position microtubule-based assemblies during cell division. This adaptor role supports higher-order developmental programs by coordinating spindle assembly and cytoskeletal remodeling at the mitotic apparatus.

A multi-pass plasma membrane cation channel in Arabidopsis that opens in response to mechanical and osmotic cues to mediate Ca2+-permeable ion flux. Its N-terminal membrane anchor and a distal seven-helix pore cooperate with a cytosolic regulatory module to couple membrane tension and osmotic gradients to channel gating. The resulting Ca2+-dependent conductance initiates cation influx and intracellular signaling, coordinating ion homeostasis and stress adaptation at the cell surface through homomeric assembly and membrane-associated scaffolding.

An intracellular ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme that forms a thioester with ubiquitin and transfers it to substrate proteins under the guidance of cognate E3 ligases. By assembling with E1 and E3 partners, it drives both mono- and polyubiquitination events that tune secretory and survival pathways. Through ubiquitin-dependent remodeling of trafficking and signaling modules, it modulates hormone release and suppresses apoptotic programs, operating primarily in soluble intracellular compartments while occasionally appearing in extracellular fractions via vesicular pathways.

A β-barrel channel of the mitochondrial outer membrane that forms a porin conduit for ions and small metabolites while serving as a high-capacity scaffold for regulatory assemblies. By anchoring at the organelle surface and recruiting cytosolic and membrane partners, it restrains intrinsic apoptosis, modulates outer-membrane biogenesis pathways, and inhibits tubulin assembly. Its membrane-embedded architecture positions it at the hub of mitochondrial–cytosolic exchange and structural coordination.

A cytoplasmic subunit of the eukaryotic chaperonin complex that uses ATP-driven conformational cycles to bind and fold non-native cytosolic proteins. By assembling into a multisubunit folding chamber, it stabilizes essential cytosolic clients and thereby sustains proteostasis pathways that indirectly shape vesicle-mediated transport and toxin handling. Its apical surface captures substrates, the equatorial core powers the cycle by nucleotide binding and hydrolysis, and the intermediate domain transmits allosteric signals that coordinate substrate capture and release.

A seven-helix membrane receptor that binds extracellular dopamine and converts this signal into intracellular second-messenger cascades by coupling to stimulatory G proteins and, in part, phospholipase C pathways. By elevating cAMP and engaging kinase networks, it modulates excitability and synaptic plasticity, shaping glutamatergic transmission and learning-related plasticity. Its activity influences neuronal development and migration in forebrain circuits, contributes to diverse motivated and stress-related behaviors, and is assembled and trafficked through intracellular compartments before functioning predominantly at postsynaptic specializations.

A mitochondrial enzyme that assembles as a crotonase-fold trimer to isomerize CoA-thioester intermediates during fatty acid degradation. It catalyzes the interconversion of trans-3-enoyl-CoA to trans-2-enoyl-CoA and rearranges conjugated Δ3,5-dienoyl-CoA to the thermodynamically favored Δ2,4-dienoyl-CoA, thereby sustaining the flow of β-oxidation for unsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids. Its soluble mitochondrial localization and propensity for multienzyme assembly enable efficient channeling of acyl-CoA intermediates through the β-oxidation pathway.

A mouse ERK-class mitogen-activated protein kinase that uses a conserved serine/threonine kinase core to transmit extracellular cues into nuclear gene-expression programs. By shuttling between cytoplasm and nucleus and accumulating in the nucleus upon activation, it phosphorylates transcriptional and regulatory substrates to coordinate morphogenesis and cell-state transitions. This signaling role aligns with functions in oocyte-associated structures such as dorsal appendages and extends to broader contexts of migration and survival governed by ERK pathway dynamics.

A nuclear transcription factor that uses a central DNA-recognition module to bind specific regulatory sequences and a C-terminal regulatory region to recruit cofactors, thereby modulating RNA polymerase II–driven gene expression. It assembles nuclear regulatory complexes on chromatin to fine-tune programs controlling maturation, differentiation, and apoptosis. By forming inhibitory assemblies that antagonize β-catenin–dependent signaling, it integrates developmental and immune cues, shaping lineage decisions in hematopoietic and skeletal systems and coordinating morphogenesis across diverse tissues.

A nuclear zinc-finger transcriptional regulator that uses a tandem array of C2H2/C2HC finger modules to bind DNA and assemble repressive protein complexes. By anchoring to specific genomic sites and recruiting chromatin-modifying assemblies, it dampens transcription of target genes and suppresses miRNA gene transcription, thereby coordinating broader gene-silencing programs within the nucleus.

A cytoplasmic enzyme in Candida glabrata that binds ATP and magnesium to drive phosphoryl/sulfur-group chemistry central to cofactor assembly. By organizing adenylate-dependent steps that feed into the formation of FMN and FAD, it sustains cellular redox metabolism and indirectly supports biofilm matrix production. Its Rossmann-like nucleotide-binding core and PAPS-reductase-like catalytic module cooperate to stabilize high-energy intermediates, enabling efficient cofactor biosynthesis in the cytosol.

A secreted extracellular glycoprotein in honeybee hemolymph that assembles into stable complexes and binds copper to support extracellular chemistry linked to innate immunity. Its hemocyanin/hexamerin architecture promotes oligomerization and matrix stabilization, enabling chloride-assisted assembly and copper-dependent tuning of pathways that generate melanin from tyrosine. By organizing and activating melanization components in the extracellular space, it enhances innate immune responses through regulated pigment formation and cross-linking.

A soluble, oligomeric bifunctional enzyme in Methanococcus maripaludis that assembles into a cytoplasmic catalytic complex and catalyzes two chemistries on basic amino acid substrates. It hydrolyzes L-ornithine to L-2-amino-4(5)-uracil and also supports ornithine cyclodeaminase and dehydrogenase reactions that generate N-acetylornithine and acrylate. By channeling nitrogen and carbon through the arginine/ornithine–uracil axis, it helps supply intermediates that feed into acrylate and acetyl pathways linked to coenzyme A biosynthesis. The enzyme operates as a homomultimer whose assembly creates two active sites and stabilizes soluble catalysis in the cytoplasm.

A membrane-associated ubiquitin ligase in mouse that operates on endosomal and trans-Golgi network membranes to assemble polyubiquitin chains on membrane cargo and adaptors. By tagging substrates that traverse early endosomes, late endosomes, and lysosomes, it accelerates cargo sorting and degradation pathways that feed antigen handling and presentation via MHC class II. Its RING-type catalytic core recruits E2 enzymes to drive ubiquitin transfer, thereby coupling ubiquitin signaling to endomembrane trafficking and immune response.

A soluble mitochondrial electron shuttle that uses a tightly bound iron–sulfur center to relay single electrons within the matrix. Its ferredoxin-like scaffold and adrenodoxin lineage enable transient complex formation with redox partners, coupling electron flow to the assembly and maintenance of mitochondrial iron–sulfur cofactors. Operating in the matrix, it likely accepts electrons from a soluble flavoprotein and donates them to membrane-associated monooxygenase systems, thereby linking redox transfer to cofactor biogenesis and mitochondrial metabolic pathways.

A soluble viral scaffold that concentrates in the host cytoplasm and assembles higher-order complexes essential for replication and immune evasion. Its N-terminal region engages nucleic acids and capsid-associated components to organize intracellular assembly pathways, while its C-terminal inhibitory module binds host innate immune factors to dampen antiviral transcriptional programs. By coordinating cytoplasmic assembly with transcriptional suppression, it stabilizes viral ribonucleoprotein complexes and supports virion production and trafficking.

A human cytosolic scaffold that assembles Rab11-driven recycling hubs to control polarized membrane trafficking. Its N-terminal membrane-targeting module anchors the complex to vesicular and cortical membranes, while a C-terminal Rab11-recognition cassette nucleates effector assemblies that couple endocytic recycling vesicles to microtubule-based transport toward the cell surface. Through dynamic cycling between cytosol, membranes, and the nucleus, it coordinates vesicle movement with transcriptional programs, thereby integrating membrane traffic and gene regulation.

A nucleoplasmic transcriptional regulator that uses a long tandem array of zinc-finger modules to anchor onto chromatin and assemble regulatory complexes. By mediating multivalent protein interactions rather than catalysis, it modulates RNA polymerase II–dependent gene expression, likely by recruiting co-regulatory and chromatin-modifying assemblies to tune promoter and enhancer activity within the nuclear interior.

A cytoplasmic enzyme that assembles and remodels nucleotide-sugar pools by catalyzing reversible guanylyl transfer between GTP/GDP and sugar phosphates. It generates GDP-D-glucose from glucose 1-phosphate and GTP and can operate in reverse to support nucleotide-sugar biosynthesis, thereby coupling glucose-6-phosphate and glucose-1-phosphate flux to activated-sugar formation within central carbohydrate metabolism.

A nucleocytoplasmic scaffold that organizes the CCR4–NOT gene-regulatory machine. Its HEAT-repeat core and multiple partner-docking modules assemble transcriptional repression and mRNA deadenylation/decay factors, channeling AU‑rich element–bound transcripts into deadenylation pathways. By coordinating complex assembly and positioning catalytic subunits, it enforces broad control of gene expression that underlies stress-responsive remodeling, including starvation- and biotic-stimulus–induced programs.

A nuclear adaptor that organizes cullin–RING ubiquitin ligase assemblies to control the abundance of chromatin-associated and RNA-processing factors. Its N-terminal substrate-recognition module captures motif-bearing targets, while central dimerization and C-terminal assembly elements recruit Cul3–RING cores to drive ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover. By tuning the stability of transcriptional and splicing regulators within the nucleus, it coordinates ubiquitin-mediated pathways that feed into gene expression and pre-mRNA processing.

A trimer-forming sodium- and potassium-permeable cation channel in zebrafish that resides at the plasma membrane and mediates amiloride-sensitive Na+ flux. Its two-helix membrane core and large extracellular domain create a selective pore whose gating and drug sensitivity are stabilized by a conserved extracellular motif. By adjusting membrane potential and downstream signaling, the channel integrates with hormone-responsive pathways that modulate epithelial and neuronal excitability through regulated surface expression and assembly.

A trimer-forming, cell-surface sodium channel that assembles as a two-pass membrane pore with a large extracellular regulatory domain to mediate sodium influx. Its gating is driven by extracellular cues rather than membrane voltage, producing sodium-selective currents that modulate cellular excitability and signaling. By shaping ion-dependent pathways that are tuned by systemic cues, it contributes to hormone-responsive physiology and operates at the plasma membrane as a multi-pass membrane protein.

A soluble bacterial translation factor that binds ribosomes and RNA via an N-terminal KOW-like platform and a C-terminal OB-fold scaffold to stimulate the elongation phase of protein synthesis. By forming a ternary complex with aminoacyl‑tRNA and elongation cofactors, it suppresses ribosome stalling and accelerates peptide elongation in thermophilic conditions. It operates primarily in the cytoplasm, with possible transient nuclear association during ribosome biogenesis, and achieves its effect through a conserved C‑terminal site that stabilizes elongation assemblies.

A Golgi-resident, single-pass type II membrane enzyme that transfers sulfate from PAPS onto heparan sulfate chains, installing 2-O-sulfation marks that shape extracellular matrix and growth-factor binding properties. By homodimerizing and operating within Golgi modification assemblies, it patterns heparan-sulfate sulfation critical for tissue patterning and contributes to limb development through its role in establishing morphogen-interacting glycans.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in mouse that uses a major facilitator superfamily core to move organic anions across epithelial membranes. Its alternating-access mechanism, characteristic of tetracycline/drug-resistance transporters, enables both apical secretion and efflux of anions and xenobiotics in polarized cells, prominently at the apical surface of renal epithelia. Cytoplasmic and nuclear-envelope–associated pools reflect biosynthesis and trafficking en route to the plasma membrane, where proton-coupled gradients drive its transport cycle.

A cytosolic adaptor that organizes motor and cytoskeletal assemblies to drive neurite and axon development in rat cells. It uses a central binding platform to assemble dynein–dynactin and kinesin transport modules along microtubules, thereby coordinating vesicle trafficking and local cytoskeletal remodeling that promote axonogenesis and extension. The same scaffold participates in centrosome- and spindle-associated events and supports nuclear envelope remodeling by recruiting membrane-remodeling and motor factors. Its soluble nature places it broadly in the cytosol, concentrating at centrosomes, the nuclear envelope, and neuronal growth cones where it stabilizes transport and assembly hubs.

A soluble RNA-binding regulator that organizes poly(A)-decorated messenger ribonucleoprotein complexes to coordinate splicing, 3′-end formation, and cytoplasmic mRNA turnover. It binds adenosine-rich RNA through a central RNA-recognition module and recruits effector proteins that balance transcript stabilization with deadenylation-dependent decay. By shuttling between nuclear splicing assemblies and cytoplasmic decay pathways, it fine-tunes mRNA fate and indirectly elevates glycoprotein biosynthesis by modulating the expression of pathways that govern protein glycosylation.

A nuclear sliding clamp that assembles into a trimeric ring encircling DNA to increase the processivity of replicative synthesis and to coordinate multiple DNA repair pathways. By providing a multivalent platform for replication and repair factors, it stabilizes polymerase engagement during rapid cell cycles and enhances genome maintenance. Its activity is expected to be most critical in proliferative blood-stage parasites, where it orchestrates replication–repair coupling within the nucleus.

A secreted trypsin-like serine endopeptidase in the African malaria mosquito that is produced as a zymogen and activated to initiate extracellular immune protease cascades. By cleaving and activating downstream targets, it amplifies innate immune pathways that drive melanization and broader defensive responses against symbionts and bacteria. Operating in hemolymph and other extracellular fluids, it promotes proteolytic processing and pathway amplification through tightly regulated activation and inhibition mechanisms.

A soluble luminal reductase that operates in acidic endocytic and lysosomal compartments to remodel disulfide-rich immune cargo and pathogen-derived proteins. By binding and processing substrates that enter via endocytosis and phagocytosis, it maintains their solubility and accessibility to degradative and presentation machinery, thereby enhancing antibacterial defense pathways. Although predominantly lysosome-associated, it functionally engages near the cell surface where uptake initiates, coordinating with membrane-proximal endocytic routes and intralysosomal processing systems.

A large cytoplasmic scaffold that binds actin via an N-terminal calponin-homology module and organizes neuron-guidance assemblies through a neuron navigator core. It promotes axon extension and broader nervous system development by coupling actin remodeling to small GTPase signaling. The scaffold concentrates at lamellipodia and filopodia and likely transiently associates with the Golgi apparatus to coordinate polarized trafficking. An internal ubiquitin-like fold and an ATPase-lid module together regulate multivalent complex assembly, enabling directional growth and cell migration.

A soluble human ubiquitination scaffold that binds conjugating enzymes and stabilizes active ligase assemblies to drive both mono- and polyubiquitination. By organizing E2–E3 modules and engaging cyclin-containing assemblies, it promotes substrate modification and self-regulation through autoubiquitination. The complex operates as a core component of soluble ubiquitin ligase assemblies that tune pathway specificity and turnover within cellular soluble pools.

A multi-pass membrane channel that assembles into a hexameric pore to conduct anions and, in alternate states, to pass nucleotides such as ATP. Its N-terminal transmembrane core forms the conduit, while a C-terminal leucine-rich repeat scaffold governs oligomerization and gating. By coupling anion flux with nucleotide movement at the plasma membrane and endomembranes, it stabilizes cellular homeostasis, modulates secretion and excitability, and influences processes including insulin secretion, myoblast differentiation, B cell development, spermatogenesis, and glucose balance.

A coiled-coil scaffold that assembles multiprotein complexes to organize microtubule-based structures in mouse cells. By concentrating binding interfaces, it recruits and stabilizes factors required for mitotic spindle assembly and also operates at the base and along the shaft of motile cilia. Cytoplasmic and cytoskeletal pools feed assembly hubs at the ciliary base and axoneme, where the scaffold coordinates nucleation and maintenance of doublet microtubules and related assemblies.

A large endocytic scaffold in mouse that oligomerizes through an N‑terminal BTB/POZ module and a central ankyrin-repeat array to assemble trafficking machinery, while a C‑terminal FYVE module targets PI3P‑rich endosomal membranes. By anchoring to endosomes and cytoplasmic vesicles, it promotes endocytosis and pinocytosis, coordinates endosomal vesicle fusion, and supports both retrograde endosome‑to‑Golgi transport and Golgi‑to‑lysosome pathways. Its mechanism relies on multivalent protein binding and membrane targeting that together organize endosomal transport routes.

A Golgi-resident, multi-pass membrane acyltransferase that installs palmitate onto cysteine residues of target proteins to control their membrane affinity, trafficking, and signaling competence. By catalyzing reversible lipidation, it modifies substrates such as the small GTPase RABL3 to tune receptor-proximal pathways and endocytic routing. Its membrane-embedded catalytic center uses acyl-CoA chemistry to drive thioester formation, thereby shaping signaling assemblies and vesicle traffic within the Golgi-centered secretory and endocytic network.

A cytoplasmic assembly scaffold that uses an extended helical repeat architecture to bind and organize protein partners involved in building the transcription apparatus. By forming multivalent oligomeric assemblies, it stabilizes and aligns components of the transcription machinery, thereby promoting efficient complex assembly and coupling to RNA handling pathways. Its mechanism centers on a tetratricopeptide-repeat solenoid that creates a high-capacity binding groove, enabling homooligomerization and cooperative assembly of transcription-related complexes.

A soluble nuclear repressor in rice that assembles oligomeric complexes to silence jasmonate-responsive genes. It uses a central oligomerization module to recruit co-repressors and chromatin modifiers, thereby enforcing transcriptional repression. Upon jasmonate perception, a C‑terminal regulatory region enables engagement with ubiquitin-ligase machinery and subsequent degradation, lifting repression and propagating the jasmonate response. The protein predominantly operates in the nucleus but can transiently associate with membrane-proximal signaling assemblies, and it may cross-regulate abscisic acid pathways through shared signaling hubs.

A large cytoplasmic scaffold that binds ubiquitin and organizes ribonucleoprotein assemblies to enhance microRNA pathway efficiency. An N-terminal ubiquitin-recognition module captures ubiquitinated partners, a central NTPase-like core provides conformational switching, and a C-terminal nuclease-like platform engages RNA-handling modules. By coupling ubiquitin-guided complex assembly with RNA-associated functions, it promotes the maturation and turnover steps that positively regulate microRNA metabolism in the cytoplasm.

A late-acting assembly factor that uses a RING-type zinc-binding scaffold to organize late-stage virion production. It operates as a soluble adaptor that shuttles between cytoplasm and nucleus, assembling viral components at membranes to drive virion assembly and budding from the plasma membrane. By forming a multivalent interaction hub rather than a catalyst, it recruits host budding machinery and coordinates membrane-associated scission to complete virion release.

A soluble, GTP-dependent carboxykinase that converts oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate, coupling GTP hydrolysis to drive gluconeogenic flux. By producing phosphoenolpyruvate from tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates, it channels carbon from mitochondrial metabolism toward glucose production. The enzyme’s two-lobed architecture binds oxaloacetate and GTP cooperatively, forming and resolving a transient phosphorylated intermediate to yield ATP and phosphoenolpyruvate. It operates in close association with mitochondrial pathways and soluble compartments to balance nucleotide use and gluconeogenic demand.

A cytoplasmic substrate-recognition subunit of an SCF ubiquitin ligase that uses an N-terminal F-box to assemble with the core ligase and a C-terminal leucine-rich repeat scaffold to capture specific targets. By presenting transcriptional regulators and cytoskeletal proteins for ubiquitination, it drives proteasome-directed turnover and can also promote monoubiquitination that modulates trafficking and signaling. Through selective targeting within inflammatory pathways, it tunes cytokine and chemokine outputs, and through actions on cytoskeletal assemblies, it shapes cell architecture and dynamics.

A cytoplasmic serine/threonine kinase in mouse that integrates signals from Rho-family GTPases to control cytoskeletal dynamics and adhesion pathways. An N-terminal GTPase-recognition module recruits and activates the kinase, which then phosphorylates targets that shape dendritic spine formation and broader neuronal morphogenesis. The enzyme operates primarily in the cytoplasm and at synaptic sites, with additional recruitment to mitochondria during stress-responsive signaling, thereby coupling extracellular cues to intracellular structural remodeling.

A large axonemal dynein motor that powers motile cilia and the sperm flagellum. Its N-terminal linker transduces ATP-driven conformational changes from a central AAA+ ATPase ring into a power stroke, while a coiled-coil stalk modulates microtubule binding to generate sliding forces between axonemal doublet microtubules. Operating within the cytoplasmic cytoskeleton of motile cilia, it drives rhythmic bending essential for cilium-based cell motility and flagellar propulsion.

A soluble adaptor that cycles between cytosol and membrane-proximal zones to terminate and rewire receptor-driven signaling. Its bipartite arrestin scaffold senses receptor-tail phosphorylation and switches into a high-affinity state that binds kinases and MAPK modules, desensitizes and internalizes G protein-coupled receptors, and assembles endocytic and degradative machinery. By scaffolding kinase and MAPK kinase complexes, it promotes ERK pathway output and modulates insulin and Notch pathways. The same assemblies transiently inhibit apoptotic cysteine proteases, thereby coupling signal transduction to cell survival. It operates predominantly in the cytosol but concentrates at actin-rich protrusions and receptor endocytic sites.

A nuclear chromatin-modifying enzyme in mouse that anchors to nucleosomes and linker DNA through H15 and winged-helix modules, reads histone states via a PHD-finger cluster, and uses a MYST acetyltransferase core to acylate chromatin-associated substrates. By assembling multivalent chromatin-bound complexes, it modulates transcriptional outputs and frequently collaborates with histone demethylases and deacetylases to stabilize repressive chromatin and dampen gene expression.

A nuclear chromatin-associated regulator that uses an N-terminal ATPase engine coupled to S5-domain scaffolding and C-terminal chromatin-reader modules to assemble and remodel meiotic chromatin. By docking onto modified nucleosomes through zinc-finger and chromo-like recognition elements, it organizes higher-order chromosome structures that drive homolog pairing, reciprocal recombination, and associated DNA repair pathways during meiosis.

A mouse cytosolic ubiquitin ligase that uses an N-terminal neuralized-repeat/SPRY scaffold to recruit substrates and endosomal adaptors and a C-terminal RING finger to catalyze ubiquitin transfer. By assembling substrate-specific ubiquitin signals, it modulates endocytic and signaling pathways and operates at early endosomes where ubiquitin tagging governs cargo sorting and vesicle maturation.

A peroxisomal oxidase that initiates β-oxidation by converting acyl‑CoA substrates to trans‑2‑enoyl‑CoA while transferring electrons to oxygen to form hydrogen peroxide. Its N‑terminal and middle domains organize FAD and acyl‑CoA binding, and its C‑terminal oxidase core reduces molecular oxygen, thereby coupling fatty acid catabolism to localized hydrogen peroxide production within the peroxisome. It likely operates in concert with other peroxisomal β‑oxidation enzymes and import machinery to manage lipid degradation and oxidative byproducts.

A secreted extracellular-matrix protein that concentrates in mineralized bone and uses a gamma-carboxylated glutamate-rich module to bind calcium and expose adhesive surfaces. By loading calcium and engaging matrix components in a calcium-dependent manner, it stabilizes and organizes the collagenous scaffold that supports hydroxyapatite deposition and maturation during bone mineralization.

A soluble thiol-dependent peroxidase that detoxifies hydrogen peroxide and organic hydroperoxides in the malaria parasite’s mitochondrion. It uses a thioredoxin-like catalytic core and a peroxiredoxin C-terminal module to perform cycles of peroxide reduction fueled by thioredoxin, thereby protecting mitochondrial components from oxidative damage. Its oligomeric transitions likely couple high-capacity peroxidase activity with stress-induced chaperoning, stabilizing redox-sensitive proteins and sustaining mitochondrial homeostasis.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in the malaria parasite that assembles a transmembrane pathway to move xenobiotics and small anions between cellular compartments and into the digestive vacuole system. It is synthesized and folded in the endoplasmic reticulum and trafficked through endocytic routes to the food vacuole, where it likely facilitates the movement of glutathione and antimalarial compounds. By coupling gradient-driven transport to vacuolar chemistry, it helps balance redox and detoxification pathways central to parasite survival.

A soluble lipid-transfer module in malaria parasite that uses a Sec14-like fold to bind and shuttle lipids between membranes. By transiently sequestering amphipathic ligands and releasing them at endosomal and secretory vesicle interfaces, it supports vesicle trafficking and tunes pathways that depend on fatty-acid–derived lipid pools. Its soluble architecture and docking surfaces enable regulated cycles of lipid capture and exchange that stabilize membrane composition and signaling during endocytic and secretory routes.

A calcium-regulated scaffolding factor in Plasmodium falciparum that assembles at parasite-induced secretory hubs within infected erythrocytes. By using a C-terminal calcium-sensing module to tune multivalent binding, it organizes complexes at Maurer’s clefts that guide exported parasite proteins through membrane-associated pathways toward the host cell surface. This assembly role coordinates cargo selection and handoff during parasite secretion and membrane translocation, with subsequent redistribution from the clefts to host cell patches and knob-associated sites.

A giant cytoplasmic scaffold that binds and organizes cytoskeletal assemblies to guide neuronal morphogenesis and restrain cell motility. An N-terminal filament-anchoring module engages actin- and microtubule-associated structures, a central navigator scaffold builds higher-order assemblies, and a C-terminal ATP-driven motor with a ubiquitin-like adaptor regulates partner binding. This architecture stabilizes and promotes microtubule growth while suppressing depolymerization, thereby dampening migratory programs and cytokine production and enabling transient coupling to nuclear-envelope–proximal regulatory hubs.

A multi-pass membrane channel that assembles into an oligomeric pore to conduct monoatomic anions and to facilitate nucleotide permeation at the cell surface. Its N-terminal transmembrane core forms the conductive pathway, while a C-terminal leucine-rich repeat scaffold stabilizes assembly and tunes gating. By operating within larger ion channel assemblies at membranes, it supports anion flux and coordinated uptake of purine nucleotides across the plasma membrane.

A cytoplasmic, cytosol-enriched E3 ubiquitin ligase that uses a RING–B-box catalytic module to assemble multivalent protein complexes, catalyze ubiquitin transfer, and undergo autoubiquitination. By modulating ubiquitin-dependent signaling assemblies, it promotes autophagy and apoptosis, likely by tuning the stability and activity of cytosolic signaling and membrane-remodeling factors that drive selective autophagic vesiculation and programmed cell death.

An ATP-dependent RNA helicase that operates in the nucleolus to remodel structured ribosomal RNA and associated ribonucleoproteins during ribosome assembly. Its helicase core uses ATP-driven conformational cycles to chaperone and transiently unwind RNA, coordinating with nucleolar biogenesis machinery to promote efficient preribosomal maturation. By sustaining ribosome production and translational capacity, it contributes to neural developmental programs in zebrafish.

A single-pass membrane receptor kinase in mouse that operates at the cell surface to transduce anti-Müllerian hormone signals. Its extracellular cystine-knot-like region organizes ligand-induced receptor assemblies, while a cytosolic serine/threonine kinase core drives phosphorylation cascades that activate a type I receptor partner and propagate TGF-beta-like signaling. Through this pathway it governs reproductive development and sex differentiation by modulating transcriptional programs at the plasma membrane.

A bifunctional enzyme that completes the terminal stages of coenzyme A assembly by first forming and then phosphorylating the immediate precursor. Its N-terminal nucleotidyltransferase-like module generates the activated intermediate, and its C-terminal P-loop kinase module executes ATP-dependent phosphate transfer to produce coenzyme A. The soluble catalytic core likely operates peripherally at the mitochondrial surface, positioning the pathway close to organelle-associated metabolism while drawing on cytosolic nucleotide pools to drive coenzyme A biogenesis.

A nuclear scaffold that organizes the 3′-end RNA-processing machinery in fruit fly. Its extended helical architecture assembles and stabilizes complexes that cleave pre-mRNAs and add poly(A) tails, and it also supports the specialized pathway that generates and matures histone mRNA precursors. By concentrating RNA-processing factors in nuclear condensates and assembling the cleavage and polyadenylation apparatus, it coordinates transcript maturation and can transiently interface with junction-associated assemblies in polarized epithelial contexts.

An accessory subunit of human mitochondrial complex I that resides on the matrix side of the inner membrane and functions as a binding-driven scaffold during assembly and stabilization of the NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase. By mediating multivalent contacts with other subunits and assembly factors, it promotes orderly construction of the respiratory supercomplex that transfers electrons from NADH to ubiquinone, thereby sustaining oxidative phosphorylation.

A nuclear scaffold that organizes homologous recombination–mediated DNA repair. Its large OB-fold–based architecture binds and stabilizes nucleic acid intermediates while recruiting repair assemblies at chromosomal damage sites. By coordinating end processing, strand invasion, and subsequent synthesis steps, it supports gap filling and the resolution of interstrand cross-links, acting at nuclear foci on chromosomes to maintain genome integrity.

A nucleoplasmic assembly factor that organizes RNA-processing complexes. An N-terminal module associated with adenine methylase pathways recruits structured RNA and methylation-coupled maturation cues, while a C-terminal MPN+/JAMM scaffold nucleates multivalent protein assemblies. Together these features enable high-capacity partner binding that supports spliceosome-driven pre-mRNA splicing and broader RNA maturation within the nucleus.

A soluble human dual-specificity phosphatase that uses a cysteine-based catalytic center to remove phosphate groups from both tyrosine and serine/threonine residues. Its catalytic core and atypical subclass features enable broad substrate recognition, allowing it to reset signaling pathways and modulate nuclear and cytoplasmic targets. By shuttling between cytoplasm and nucleus, it fine-tunes phosphorylation-dependent circuits through a covalent phosphoenzyme mechanism, thereby coordinating reversible dephosphorylation in both compartments.

An ATP-driven RNA-remodeling enzyme that uses a DEAD-box helicase core and a ribosome-biogenesis–specialized C-terminal extension to unwind and refold structured ribosomal RNA during assembly. It operates primarily in the nucleolus and nucleoplasm, with a soluble pool in the cytosol, where it transiently binds RNA and assembly factors to promote rRNA processing and preribosomal complex maturation through iterative ATP-coupled remodeling cycles.

A single-pass cell-surface adhesion receptor that forms a heterodimeric integrin complex to mediate high-affinity attachment to extracellular matrix and stabilize cell-cell contacts. Its extracellular head and stalk bind matrix ligands and transmit conformational signals that regulate affinity and clustering, while the cytoplasmic tail recruits adaptor proteins to couple adhesion to actin assembly and focal adhesion machinery. Through this bidirectional signaling, it coordinates migration, stress fiber formation, epithelial adhesion, and developmental programs, operating at the plasma membrane within integrin assemblies and integrating with growth factor pathways.

A secreted spider venom factor that inhibits voltage-gated potassium channels by binding their extracellular vestibules to collapse outward currents, and that additionally perturbs anionic membranes to produce reversible depolarization and, at higher concentrations, irreversible membrane damage. Acting in the extracellular milieu, it suppresses ion-channel-dependent excitability and contributes to broader defensive roles against surface-exposed organisms, consistent with a soluble, membrane-interactive toxin that shapes prey and predator physiology.

A cytoplasmic DENN-scaffolded exchange factor that activates small GTPases controlling endosomal maturation. By catalyzing nucleotide exchange on endosomal GTPases, it transiently binds and activates the machinery that drives vesicle-mediated and protein transport along the endocytic route. This activity tunes the transition from early to late endosomes and promotes entry of cargo into the multivesicular body pathway, with functional concentration at late endosomes through Rab-dependent recruitment.

A single-pass membrane-anchored RING E3 ligase that assembles polyubiquitin chains on membrane-associated complexes to control antigen presentation. By binding and ubiquitinating MHC class II assemblies at endosomal and lysosomal interfaces, it routes incomplete loading intermediates toward degradation and thereby tunes peptide presentation and immune responsiveness. The catalytic core resides on the cytosolic face of endomembranes, where it recruits ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes and collaborates with trafficking machinery to couple ubiquitin signaling to endosomal sorting and lysosomal turnover.

A cytoplasmic axonemal dynein motor that powers sperm flagellar beating. Its AAA+ ATPase ring hydrolyzes ATP to drive conformational changes in a lever-like linker, while a coiled-coil stalk engages axonemal microtubules to convert chemical energy into sliding and bending of doublet filaments. By assembling into dynein arms within the flagellum, it generates the waveform and propulsion essential for motility in human sperm.

A soluble isoprenoid-reducing enzyme in Methanosarcina acetivorans that uses a flavin- and NAD(P)H-dependent catalytic core to hydrogenate double bonds in geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate and digeranylgeranylglycerophospholipid. By saturating isoprenoid chains, it contributes to membrane-lipid tailoring and broader lipid modification pathways. The enzyme operates primarily in the cytoplasm, where it accesses soluble redox cofactors, and may transiently interface with archaeal mitochondrial-like compartments that intersect lipid metabolism. Its mechanism centers on hydride transfer from NAD(P)H through a bound flavin to the isoprenoid substrate, stabilizing and reducing the double-bond chemistry.

A small cytoplasmic adaptor that is essential for chemotaxis and associated with growth inhibition. It uses a compact YjiS-like scaffold to assemble transient protein complexes that tune chemotaxis signaling and motility, with pronounced enrichment at the division plane. By organizing partner proteins in the cytoplasm and at the septum, it coordinates taxis with cell-cycle and cytoskeletal modules to modulate growth and environmental response.

A small, soluble adaptor that concentrates at bacterial septa and organizes virulence-associated assemblies that favor tumor induction. By using a compact interaction module to bind partner proteins, it nucleates complexes that attenuate host programmed cell death and apoptosis. Its septal enrichment suggests a role in staging and delivering virulence machinery and effectors at cell division-associated hubs, thereby creating a cellular environment permissive for successful host manipulation.

A multi-pass membrane scaffold in mouse that assembles endosomal and cytoskeletal complexes to sustain axon formation and broader neuronal morphogenesis. By organizing trafficking and structural modules on endosomal membranes, it coordinates membrane supply and cytoskeletal remodeling that drive neurite outgrowth and cell migration. Its scaffolded interaction capacity supports lipid balance and endosomal dynamics, positioning it as a key regulator of neuron projection development and axonogenesis.

A soluble dual-specificity phosphatase in mouse that uses a cysteine-dependent catalytic center to remove phosphate groups from tyrosine and serine/threonine residues on target proteins. By engaging and dephosphorylating components of the ERK pathway, it dampens MAPK signaling and thereby modulates cell survival versus apoptosis decisions. The enzyme operates primarily in the cytoplasm but likely accesses the nucleus to act on shuttling substrates and transcriptional regulators, using transient binding interfaces to assemble with signaling complexes and fine-tune pathway flux.

A soluble human phosphatase that uses a cysteine-dependent catalytic center to hydrolyze phosphomonoesters and assemble regulatory complexes across the cytoplasm, mitochondria, and nucleus. By shuttling between these compartments, it modulates phosphorylation-dependent pathways that govern intrinsic apoptosis and transcriptional control. Its dual-specificity catalytic module and family identity suggest coupling of protein and lipid phosphate removal, positioning the enzyme as a hub that binds partners to position substrates and tune mitochondrial and nuclear signaling circuits.

A multi-pass membrane acyltransferase that installs long-chain fatty acyl groups onto cysteine residues of target proteins, thereby tuning their membrane affinity, trafficking, and signaling. It catalyzes palmitoylation via a zinc-coordinated active site that forms a transient acyl-enzyme intermediate, modifies substrates such as NRAS and MYC, and functions predominantly at endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi membranes with a soluble-facing catalytic loop and occasional nuclear-associated pools. By coupling membrane anchoring with selective substrate recognition, it orchestrates reversible lipidation that gates assembly of signaling and trafficking complexes.

A basolateral, multi-pass membrane symporter that uses the sodium gradient to drive concentrative uptake of dicarboxylates and other organic anions, prominently including succinate and glutathione. By coupling sodium binding to alternating-access transport, it elevates intracellular pools of these metabolites, thereby supporting energy metabolism and redox balance. Its membrane-embedded architecture and basolateral enrichment position it at the epithelial interface, with a fraction trafficked through extracellular vesicles that reflect membrane turnover and intercellular communication.

A small regulatory GTPase that cycles between GTP- and GDP-bound states to control membrane trafficking between the Golgi and endosomal systems. By switching conformations, it recruits effectors and tethers that guide vesicle budding, transport, and fusion, thereby tuning receptor and cargo flow that feeds into broader signaling pathways and developmental programs. It dynamically partitions between the cytoplasm and cytoplasmic vesicle membranes through reversible membrane association characteristic of Rab proteins.

A soluble cytoplasmic ATP-dependent citrate-cleaving enzyme that generates cytosolic acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate. By coupling citrate capture to ATP-driven acyl transfer and thioester chemistry, it supplies acetyl units that feed membrane lipid assembly, cholesterol and broader isoprenoid pathways. Its multi-lobed architecture coordinates citrate, coenzyme A, and adenylate to channel acetyl-CoA toward phospholipid and sterol biosynthesis, likely operating near organelle interfaces while functioning as a soluble catalyst in the cytoplasm.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in mouse that concentrates citrate and succinate into cells by coupling their uptake to the inward sodium gradient. Its transmembrane core forms an alternating-access pathway that captures dicarboxylates and other small organic anions at the membrane interface, releasing them into the cytosol to support central carbon metabolism and signaling. The transporter’s activity integrates with sodium-driven energy transduction and is expected to reside at the plasma membrane where sodium gradients are maintained.

A Golgi-anchored, single-pass type II membrane glycosyltransferase that installs terminal sialic acid onto maturing glycoconjugates. Its luminal catalytic domain uses CMP–sialic acid to build α2→3 linkages on glycoprotein substrates and can extend acceptor glycans that already bear α2→3 or α2→6 sialylation. By finalizing sialylation during secretory pathway transit, it completes protein glycosylation and thereby influences the composition and properties of glycoproteins that are subsequently displayed at the cell surface and secreted into extracellular compartments.

A membrane-embedded flavocytochrome that uses a cytosolic FAD/NADPH-reducing module coupled to a multi-pass transmembrane redox core to transfer electrons from NADPH to oxygen, generating superoxide and downstream hydrogen peroxide at membrane and perinuclear interfaces. By concentrating reactive oxygen species at the plasma membrane, apical surface, and endoplasmic reticulum, it modulates apoptosis, stress responses, cytoskeletal and adhesion assemblies, and cell migration. Its trafficking and scaffolding with cytoskeletal and adhesion systems position it to tune hypoxia and growth factor pathways through localized redox signaling.

A cytoplasmic serine/threonine kinase that uses a conserved catalytic core to phosphorylate protein substrates and assemble regulatory complexes controlling stress adaptation and membrane trafficking. By tuning endocytosis and receptor internalization, it coordinates oxidative stress responses and intracellular transport, and it modulates autophagy and ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis. Its signaling also dampens specific potassium and calcium transport pathways. The enzyme operates predominantly in the cytoplasm and transiently at spindle structures during meiotic and mitotic programs, where phosphorylation events couple cytoskeletal dynamics to broader cellular regulation.

A nuclear chromatin-modifying enzyme that binds linker-associated and nucleosomal chromatin through N‑terminal winged-helix and H1/H5-like modules and a PHD-finger reader, then uses a MYST acetyltransferase core to acetylate histone H3. By coupling chromatin targeting with acetyl-CoA–dependent acetylation, it remodels nucleosome structure and assembles regulatory complexes that can repress transcription at selected genomic loci.

A soluble, switch-like regulator of membrane trafficking that cycles between GTP- and GDP-bound states to control vesicle transport. It assembles and disassembles effector complexes that govern endocytic and secretory pathways, acting at cytoplasmic interfaces and the plasma membrane. Predominantly cytoplasmic when inactive, it transiently associates with membranes during cargo sorting and vesicle movement, thereby tuning intracellular transport through regulated protein interactions.

A small ARF-like GTPase in C. elegans that operates as a nucleotide-controlled switch at the endoplasmic reticulum. By cycling between GTP- and GDP-bound states, it assembles and remodels ER-associated protein complexes that tune the unfolded protein response. This switchable scaffold likely coordinates chaperone and adaptor systems to balance folding and degradation pathways during ER stress, thereby modulating the magnitude and timing of stress-adaptive signaling.

A human multi-pass membrane scaffold that assembles homooligomeric complexes on lysosomal membranes to regulate gene expression. By forming stable oligomers and recruiting cytosolic factors at the lysosome, it modulates RNA stability and biases transcriptional output toward repression. Its architecture favors membrane-tethered assemblies that coordinate endolysosomal trafficking with cytoplasmic and nuclear regulatory pathways, thereby tuning RNA and transcriptional homeostasis from a lysosomal platform.

A human multi-pass membrane transporter that uses an alternating-access mechanism to expel diverse xenobiotics and drugs, thereby conferring multidrug resistance and supporting detoxification. It concentrates at the apical surface of polarized cells, where outward efflux protects tissues by clearing compounds into luminal spaces. Cytosolic loops likely recruit ubiquitin ligases that regulate endocytosis and surface residency, and biosynthetic and quality-control steps occur in cytoplasmic and perinuclear membrane compartments before apical delivery.

A human multi-pass membrane transporter that assembles a sodium-coupled alternating-access pore to move amphipathic anions at the cell surface. Its architecture supports vectorial transport that contributes to hormone handling and bile acid–like metabolite trafficking. Cytosolic loops and termini provide docking sites for regulatory proteins that tune membrane residency and activity, situating the transporter at the plasma membrane where it integrates sodium gradients with endogenous solute uptake and release.

A mitochondrial membrane-associated exchange platform that uses an RCC1-like beta-propeller to catalyze nucleotide exchange on small GTPases and to scaffold multiprotein assemblies. By activating membrane-proximal GTPase pathways, it coordinates outer-membrane fusion with inner-membrane organization and supports mitochondrial ribosome function. Its RNA-binding capacity and assembly role align membrane remodeling with enhanced mitochondrial translation, integrating fusion machinery and biosynthetic output at the organelle surface.

A soluble mitochondrial enzyme subunit that specifies nucleotide handling within the succinyl-CoA synthetase complex of the tricarboxylic acid cycle. By shaping the nucleotide-binding and phosphate-transfer environment, it enables reversible interconversion among succinyl-CoA, succinate, and guanine nucleotides, thereby coupling carbon flux to mitochondrial GTP/GDP pools. Operating in the mitochondrial matrix, it assembles with partner subunits to drive substrate-level phosphorylation and coordinates with neighboring steps of central metabolism through multivalent protein interactions.

A nucleocytoplasmic RNA-binding regulator that recognizes methylated adenosine marks on transcripts and assembles ribonucleoprotein complexes to control pre-mRNA processing. By selectively engaging m6A-modified RNAs and recruiting splicing machinery, it promotes spliceosome-dependent exon choice in the nucleus and likely influences cytoplasmic RNA fate through transient shuttling and assembly with RNA-processing factors.

A human endoplasmic reticulum membrane subunit of the GPI-anchor assembly pathway that acts as a multi-pass binding scaffold within the transamidase machinery. By organizing and stabilizing the complex that transfers glycosylphosphatidylinositol to substrate proteins, it promotes efficient anchor formation and handoff in the ER. Its membrane-embedded architecture positions partner proteins and substrates to drive the GPI-anchor biosynthetic process and maintain the integrity of the transamidase assembly.

A secreted fungal endo-β-1,3-glucanase that depolymerizes extracellular β-1,3-glucans by cleaving internal linkages, generating soluble oligosaccharides that feed carbohydrate metabolism. Its N-terminal catalytic core and C-terminal lectin-like module cooperate to bind and hydrolyze β-glucan chains, supporting nutrient acquisition from environmental polysaccharides such as laminarin and laminariolysis in the extracellular milieu.

An archaeal translation initiation factor that assembles with other initiation components to promote early steps of protein synthesis. It uses a modular scaffold to bind partner proteins and stabilize initiator tRNA placement on the ribosome, thereby advancing the formation of the initiation complex. The factor operates primarily in the cytoplasm, with transient association to membrane-proximal ribosome assemblies and occasional nuclear-related locales where RNA–protein complexes concentrate. Its mechanism relies on multivalent protein interactions that rigidify and position the initiation machinery for accurate start-site selection.

An archaeal rRNA-modifying enzyme that binds structured small-subunit rRNA and transfers a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to a defined nucleotide within the 5S rRNA pathway. By recognizing and stabilizing assembly intermediates, it promotes maturation of the small ribosomal subunit and coordinates checkpoint steps in ribosome biogenesis. The enzyme likely functions as a soluble oligomer associated with the nucleoid, where it engages pre-ribosomal particles to ensure precise rRNA base methylation and structural stabilization.

An archaeal translation-initiation scaffold that organizes early steps of protein synthesis by binding partner factors and ribosomal RNA to position initiator tRNA at the ribosome. Its N-terminal nucleic acid–binding fold anchors to RNA, while central and C-terminal regions stabilize assemblies with initiation partners and ribosomal surfaces in the cytoplasm. By nucleating the pre-initiation complex and coordinating factor recruitment, it drives initiation and can transiently interface with RNA-centric assemblies that viruses co-opt during their transcriptional cycles.

A cytoplasmic initiation-factor GTPase that assembles and remodels translation initiation complexes in archaeal ribosomes. Its N-terminal GTP-binding engine drives conformational switching, while central beta-barrel and C-terminal modules scaffold partner binding and ribosome engagement. In the GTP-bound state it stabilizes ternary assemblies that recruit initiator tRNA and organize small-subunit loading; hydrolysis triggers complex turnover and factor recycling. Through this assembly-centric mechanism it anchors the initiation stage of protein synthesis and interfaces with downstream elongation within cytoplasmic translation assemblies.

A soluble viral RNA end-processing enzyme that assembles in the cytoplasm to convert 5′-triphosphorylated RNA and small nucleotide triphosphates into diphosphate products, thereby priming viral transcripts for cap formation and efficient accumulation. Its metal-dependent catalytic core hydrolyzes terminal phosphates and is allosterically tuned by ATP and GTP binding and hydrolysis, coupling nucleotide energy states to RNA triphosphatase activity. Operating within a cytoplasmic transferase assembly, it collaborates with a viral RNA ligase and capping machinery to drive high-output mRNA production from the viral genome.

A cytosolic enzyme that generates selenophosphate by coupling ATP and inorganic phosphate chemistry within a two-lobed catalytic core. By producing the activated selenium donor required for selenocysteine formation and selenoprotein assembly, it drives selenium flux into amino acid–related pathways. The PurM-like N- and C-terminal lobes assemble an interdomain active site that binds ATP and coordinates metal ions to execute reversible phosphotransfer, positioning the enzyme as a central supplier of selenophosphate in the cytosol.

A mitochondrial thiol–disulfide oxidoreductase that uses a thioredoxin catalytic center to bind assembly factors and assembly intermediates, maintaining cysteine residues in a reduced state to promote maturation of oxidative phosphorylation machinery. By supporting the formation and stability of respiratory complexes—particularly complex I—it sustains electron transfer from NADH to ubiquinone. Its soluble mitochondrial pool likely operates through cycles of dithiol–disulfide exchange, transiently engaging assembly modules to couple redox chemistry to respiratory chain biogenesis.

A basolateral, multi-pass membrane transporter in rat epithelia that uses a major facilitator superfamily core to drive secondary active uptake of bulky amphipathic organic anions. It concentrates diverse substrates—including bile acids, conjugated steroids, thyroid hormones, prostaglandins, and fatty acids—across the basolateral plasma membrane to support hepatic and renal epithelial physiology. An extracellular Kazal-like loop likely modulates substrate access and stabilizes the outward-facing vestibule, while cytosolic loops and trafficking pathways maintain basolateral residency and high-capacity transport.

An extracellular adhesion scaffold in Toxoplasma gondii that uses a long array of calcium-binding EGF repeats, stabilized by hydroxylation, to assemble high-avidity adhesive complexes at cell-cell interfaces. By rigidifying its EGF architecture and clustering at junction-like sites, it promotes homotypic adhesion and selective recognition between similar cells, organizing multicellular assemblies and stabilizing contact zones through multivalent protein binding.

A cytoplasmic regulatory scaffold that uses multivalent protein binding to coordinate membrane-proximal assemblies and nuclear organization. By positioning itself at membrane–cytoskeleton interfaces through a conserved C-terminal targeting module, it assembles complexes that guide cargo and regulatory factors toward membrane compartments and the nucleus. This spatial control supports survival and differentiation pathways and promotes local desumoylation by recruiting SUMO-pathway enzymes, thereby tuning nuclear architecture and associated trafficking circuits.

A small multi-pass membrane adaptor that tethers cAMP-dependent protein kinase assemblies to membrane-proximal sites and transiently to cytosolic and nuclear compartments. By concentrating kinase and phosphatase modules into defined signaling nanodomains, it modulates phosphorylation circuits that can either stimulate or inhibit distinct PKA-driven pathways and thereby biases cellular programs toward proliferation. Its mechanism relies on multivalent protein binding that organizes membrane-associated signaling hubs while dynamically sampling soluble and nuclear environments.

A soluble pyrophosphohydrolase that assembles via an N-terminal regulatory module and a C-terminal catalytic core to hydrolyze ADP-ribose and other nucleoside diphosphate–linked metabolites. It primarily operates in the mitochondrial matrix to maintain nucleotide and energy balance by converting ADP-ribose into AMP and ribose-5-phosphate, while additional pools in the nucleoplasm and nuclear bodies tune ADP-ribose–dependent nuclear assemblies. Its protein-binding surfaces support transient complexes that position the enzyme at mitochondrial and nuclear interfaces, with peripheral associations at cell junctions and within vesicular pathways.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator that uses an N-terminal repression module and a C-terminal array of zinc fingers to anchor at specific genomic sites and assemble a silencing complex. By recruiting corepressor machinery and positioning it on chromatin, it dampens RNA polymerase II–driven transcription within the nucleoplasm and can transiently associate with nucleolar chromatin. This mechanism couples sequence-directed chromatin targeting to assembly of repressive protein complexes that fine-tune gene expression programs.

A soluble human serine/threonine kinase that binds ATP and transfers phosphate to diverse protein substrates, coordinating signaling pathways that govern cell-cycle control and broader phosphorylation cascades. It operates in both the cytoplasm and nucleoplasm, where docking-driven assemblies guide substrate selection and timing. By shuttling between compartments, it integrates cytosolic signaling with nuclear checkpoint and transcriptional programs to modulate progression through the cell cycle.

A cell-surface, single-pass type I membrane protein whose extracellular leucine-rich repeat scaffold binds both proteins and ceramide to organize adhesion and signaling assemblies. By clustering adhesion complexes and sphingolipid-enriched membrane microdomains at the external face of the plasma membrane, it promotes epithelial cohesion and coordinates inward signaling that enhances Rho-dependent pathways controlling cytoskeletal and junctional dynamics. Its maturation proceeds through the secretory pathway and it can be incorporated into extracellular vesicles.

A cytoplasmic adaptor that uses an N-terminal RWD fold and a C-terminal GIR2/ZC3H15/TMA46-family module to assemble stress-responsive and signaling complexes. By scaffolding multiprotein assemblies rather than catalyzing reactions, it enhances androgen receptor pathway throughput and indirectly boosts transcription factor activity, particularly under oxidative stress. Its soluble architecture positions it to coordinate hormone and stress signaling in the cytoplasm, thereby tuning downstream transcriptional outputs.

A soluble cytoskeletal adaptor that assembles higher-order complexes to regulate microtubule-based events during cell division and neurodevelopment. By homodimerizing and scaffolding dynein–dynactin–LIS1 regulatory modules at centrosomes and spindle poles, it organizes the mitotic spindle, ensures proper spindle orientation, and supports accurate chromosome segregation. Its cytoplasmic, cytoskeleton-associated localization concentrates at centrosomes and spindle structures, where it coordinates force generation and microtubule anchoring to drive mitotic fidelity and contribute to cortical development.

A conformationally switchable adaptor that uses a HORMA fold to assemble and regulate multivalent protein complexes controlling cell-cycle checkpoints, DNA repair pathway choice, and transcriptional programs. By clamping onto short motifs on partner proteins, it stabilizes assemblies at centromeres and near the anaphase-promoting complex to restrain proteolysis during the spindle checkpoint. It coordinates responses to DNA damage by biasing repair toward end joining and tempering homologous recombination, while modulating kinase signaling, ubiquitin pathways, and transcription. The protein shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm, concentrating at chromosomal and checkpoint hubs to integrate mitotic control with broader growth, adhesion, cytoskeletal, and immune-related processes.

A nuclear RNA-binding regulator that couples transcription with pre-mRNA maturation. Its N-terminal RNA-recognition module captures nascent transcripts and regulatory nucleic acids, while a C-terminal interaction-rich tail recruits assembly factors. By anchoring to chromatin and promoter–enhancer regions, it stabilizes RNA polymerase II–dependent transcription and coordinates assembly of splice-regulatory ribonucleoprotein complexes, thereby promoting transcription and pre-mRNA processing.

A soluble bifunctional enzyme in mouse that completes the final stages of coenzyme A assembly. Its N-terminal nucleotidyltransferase-like module forms an adenylyl intermediate that generates the dephospho-CoA precursor, and its C-terminal P-loop kinase module then phosphorylates this intermediate to produce coenzyme A. By coupling adenylyl transfer and phosphate transfer in sequence, it sustains cellular pools of coenzyme A required for acyl-transfer chemistry. The enzyme operates primarily in soluble compartments and can access nuclear regions where coenzyme A–dependent acylation pathways intersect with transcriptional control.

An endoplasmic reticulum–resident, multi-pass membrane enzyme that catalyzes the first mannose addition during assembly of glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchors. By transferring mannose from a lipid-linked donor to the nascent GPI anchor, it commits secretory-pathway proteins to membrane attachment and drives their maturation and surface display. Its membrane-embedded catalytic core operates within ER assembly lines that feed GPI-anchored protein biogenesis and broader cell-surface organization.

A soluble cytoplasmic enzyme that catalyzes stereoinversion of an unnatural amino acid derived from a prenylated pyrimidine, thereby supplying the correctly configured building block required for assembly of the aurescenside antibiotic pathway in Paenarthrobacter. Its racemase-like fold supports a two-base proton-transfer mechanism that edits stereochemistry and channels flux into specialized peptide/peptidyl antibiotic biosynthesis.

A calcium-gated serine/threonine kinase in Arabidopsis that integrates intracellular calcium transients into phosphorylation signals at the cell surface. Its N-terminal catalytic core is activated by a C-terminal EF-hand regulatory module that binds calcium and unlocks the kinase active site. By residing at the plasma membrane, it converts calcium spikes into substrate phosphorylation that modulates membrane-associated signaling pathways central to calcium-responsive cellular programs.

A nuclear speckle–resident regulator of pre-mRNA splicing that uses an N-terminal organizing module and a central RS-like interaction platform to assemble ribonucleoprotein complexes and tune splice-site choice. By coupling multivalent RNA and protein binding, it concentrates spliceosomal machinery within nuclear speckles and the surrounding nucleoplasm, thereby modulating alternative splicing pathways that feed into broader developmental programs.

A multi-pass membrane glycosyltransferase in human cells that installs the first mannose onto glycosylphosphatidylinositol precursors during anchor assembly. Operating within the endoplasmic reticulum, it uses lipid-linked mannose donors to catalyze mannose transfer at the membrane–lumen interface, thereby initiating and driving the GPI biosynthetic pathway that ultimately tethers numerous proteins to membranes.

A cytoplasmic scaffold that organizes stress-responsive and receptor-signaling assemblies. Its N-terminal interaction module and C-terminal GIR2/TMA46-family region cooperate to bind multiple partners, stabilize higher-order complexes, and tune cytoplasmic pathways. Through this adaptor architecture, it buffers oxidative stress responses, enhances signaling receptor activity, and potentiates transcription factor function within androgen receptor–dependent pathways.

A soluble eukaryotic adenylyltransferase that assembles into homo-oligomers and catalyzes ATP-dependent formation of NAD+ from nicotinamide mononucleotide and, in parallel, NaAD from sodium nicotinamide mononucleotide. By sustaining nuclear NAD+/NaAD pools, it supports nucleotide biosynthesis and adenylate metabolism. Its oligomeric architecture concentrates activity within nuclear substructures, where local NAD regeneration stabilizes transcriptional and chromatin-associated demands.

A human HECT-type ubiquitin ligase that uses an N-terminal membrane-targeting module and central WW repeats to recruit PY-motif-bearing substrates and adaptors, then employs a C-terminal catalytic module to transfer ubiquitin and remodel signaling and transcriptional circuits. By assembling with itself and other ligase subunits, it attenuates TGF-beta/BMP pathways, modulates canonical and planar cell polarity branches of Wnt signaling, and represses RNA polymerase II–driven transcription. These activities drive ubiquitin-dependent protein turnover and shape developmental and migratory programs in cytosolic and nuclear speck compartments.

A soluble mitochondrial elongation factor that forms a dimeric platform to chaperone the elongation cycle of organellar protein synthesis. By remodeling and activating the mitochondrial translational GTPase and stabilizing delivery of aminoacyl‑tRNA to the ribosomal A site, it sustains efficient peptide elongation within the mitochondrial matrix. Its dimerization core enforces the conformational states required for nucleotide exchange and ternary complex handling, thereby coupling factor recycling to ongoing mitochondrial translation.

An archaeal cytoskeletal organizer that assembles and stabilizes the salin cell. It uses a salactin-based scaffold to bind and arrange filamentous lattice structures and a nucleotide-binding core that modulates assembly dynamics. By coupling structural binding with an energy-tunable switch, it promotes formation and maintenance of the membrane-associated cytoskeletal compartment essential for intracellular organelle assembly in Halobacterium.

A cytosolic ATP-dependent ligase that assembles a key peptidoglycan precursor by joining L-glutamate to the UDP-linked tetrapeptide backbone. Its modular catalytic core activates a carboxylate and aligns the amino acid acceptor to form an amide bond, thereby advancing the cytosolic route that supplies building blocks for cell-wall construction. By transiently associating with other soluble pathway enzymes, it channels intermediates toward envelope biogenesis and sustains the flow of precursors required for robust peptidoglycan assembly.

A calcium-regulated signaling and trafficking factor that uses an EF-hand–driven conformational switch to bind heterotrimeric G-protein alpha subunits and receptor complexes, thereby coupling intracellular calcium sensing to hormone and nutrient signaling. It operates in the cytoplasm and Golgi medial cisterna and is also released to the extracellular space, where it modulates endocrine pathways. By tuning exchange-factor chemistry and receptor interactions, it shapes insulin and peptide hormone signaling, coordinates responses to glucose and starvation, and influences appetite, adipocyte differentiation, fatty acid metabolism, and steroidogenic pathways.

A soluble cytoplasmic condensing enzyme that initiates acetyl-dependent precursor flow by forming a beta-ketoacyl intermediate through a thiolase-like catalytic core. This chemistry seeds fatty acid–type II pathways and, in actinobacteria, redirects acetyl flux toward isoprenoid production via the methylerythritol phosphate route. By transiently forming an acyl-enzyme and driving a Claisen condensation that commits carbon into downstream branches, it integrates acetyl-CoA metabolism with isoprenoid precursor supply in the cytoplasm.

A soluble serine/threonine kinase that uses a canonical catalytic core and an AGC-type regulatory tail to assemble and activate phosphorylation cascades controlling diverse cellular programs. It operates predominantly in the cytoplasm but is dynamically recruited to plasma membrane signaling hubs and shuttles to the nucleus to modify transcriptional regulators. By binding other kinases and scaffolds, it integrates oxidative, hypoxic, and wound cues, driving stress-adaptive phosphorylation pathways and, under sustained challenge, promoting programmed cell death.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in Plasmodium that assembles a selective conduit for small-molecule flux along the endoplasmic reticulum–food vacuole axis. It likely handles xenobiotic compounds and mobilizes glutathione and related thiol conjugates, thereby tuning the chemical environment of the digestive compartment and contributing to drug tolerance and thiol-dependent detoxification. The protein is synthesized and folded in the endoplasmic reticulum before trafficking to internal membranes, where its alternating-access mechanism supports solute movement essential for parasite physiology.

A large intracellular calcium-release channel in Dictyostelium that uses an extensive cytosolic regulatory scaffold to bind calcium and inositol phosphates and trigger Ca2+ flux from intracellular membranes. By generating localized calcium signals, it coordinates cytoskeletal remodeling and adhesion dynamics that underlie cell-cell adhesion and cell migration, and it likely couples calcium signaling to RNA-processing assemblies through its armadillo-like scaffold. The protein is a single-pass type I membrane protein positioned on intracellular vesicle membranes with potential transient association near the cell surface.

A human intracellular redox enzyme that assembles a membrane-embedded heme conduit with a cytosolic flavin/NADPH engine to transfer electrons from NADPH to oxygen and generate superoxide. By producing reactive oxygen species at intracellular membranes, it drives signaling that shapes inflammatory pathways, modulates transcriptional programs, and contributes to cardiac physiology. Its redox activity also interfaces with sulfur amino acid handling, consistent with a role in homocysteine-related metabolism. The membrane-anchored architecture and soluble cofactor-binding modules together specify a multi-pass membrane oxidase whose activity is tightly coupled to intracellular signaling networks.

A soluble nuclear RNA-modifying enzyme that uses a SAM-dependent catalytic core and a C-terminal CCCH zinc finger to bind and chemically modify tRNA. It installs an N7-methyl group on guanine within tRNA, stabilizing the tRNA structure and supporting accurate translation. Operating within the nucleoplasm, it likely engages RNA-processing assemblies to couple precise tRNA recognition with efficient methyl transfer during maturation.

A cytosolic cytoskeleton-associated adaptor that oligomerizes through a central NUDE scaffold to organize assemblies controlling spindle orientation and chromosome positioning during mitosis. By recruiting and tuning dynein–dynactin and related regulators at centrosomes and kinetochores, it helps orient the mitotic spindle and stabilize chromosome localization in dividing cells. Dynamic recruitment from the cytosol to membrane-proximal sites and mitotic structures supports neural progenitor divisions that contribute to cerebral cortex development.

A cytosolic enzyme that initiates and drives a key radical chemistry step in molybdenum cofactor assembly. Its N-terminal radical SAM core binds an iron–sulfur cluster and uses SAM-dependent radical initiation to remodel a linear precursor into a cyclic pyranopterin intermediate, while a C-terminal partner module organizes and channels intermediates within the pathway. Through lyase-like transformations that involve both carbon–carbon and phosphorus–oxygen bond chemistry, it supplies the essential cyclic intermediate that feeds forward into molybdenum-cofactor maturation in the cytosol.

A cytoplasmic signaling scaffold and guanine-nucleotide exchange catalyst that assembles receptor- and G-protein–derived inputs into Rho-family GTPase activation. An N-terminal PDZ module recruits membrane receptor/channel tails, a central RGS-like region organizes heterotrimeric G-protein signaling, and a C-terminal catalytic core uses a DH-PH tandem to activate small GTPases at phosphoinositide-rich membranes. By coupling these pathways, it modulates cytoskeletal and vesicle-trafficking circuits that tune neurotransmitter handling and operates at membrane-proximal cytoplasm and contractile fiber assemblies.

A single-pass cell-surface adhesion receptor that presents a long cadherin-like ectodomain to mediate calcium-stiffened homophilic binding between neighboring cells and a cytoplasmic tail that recruits intracellular scaffolds. By coupling extracellular adhesion to intracellular adaptor assembly, it organizes cell–cell cohesion and transduces signals at the plasma membrane, thereby shaping intercellular junctions and adhesion-dependent pathways.

A soluble mitochondrial enzyme subunit that builds the nucleotide-handling core of succinyl-CoA synthetase in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Its ATP-grasp scaffold and beta-subunit architecture confer ADP/ATP specificity and organize phosphate-transfer chemistry that converts succinyl-CoA to succinate while generating ATP in the matrix. By assembling with its partner subunits and neighboring metabolic machinery, it channels succinyl-CoA flux and stabilizes nucleotide balance within mitochondria.

A cell-surface, multi-pass chemokine-receptor scaffold in mouse that binds diverse chemokines with high affinity and modulates their availability and signaling at the plasma membrane. By capturing chemokines extracellularly and favoring receptor-mediated internalization and sorting over strong G-protein signaling, it dampens and reshapes chemokine-driven pathways that govern inflammatory responses and chemokine output. This membrane-embedded mechanism positions the receptor at the external face of the plasma membrane to intercept soluble chemokines and fine-tune endothelial and immune signaling circuits.

A soluble, two-module enzyme that couples a phospho-motif–recognition WW domain to a peptidyl-prolyl isomerase catalytic core to remodel phosphorylation-dependent substrates. By first capturing Ser/Thr–proline–containing targets and then catalyzing cis–trans isomerization of proline bonds, it switches client conformations to control mitotic timing and cytokinesis, stabilize or turnover specific proteins, and tune signaling pathways including canonical Wnt and amyloidogenic routes. It operates in both cytosol and nucleus and is recruited to neuronal circuits, where it supports synapse organization and differentiation programs.

A nucleocytoplasmic RNA-binding regulator that reads N6-methyladenosine marks to coordinate post-transcriptional gene control. It binds m6A-containing RNAs through a conserved recognition module and assembles with processing machineries to enhance pre-mRNA splicing in the nucleus. After export, it associates with cytoplasmic assemblies that promote mRNA storage and turnover, thereby coupling nuclear splicing with downstream fate decisions through multivalent protein interactions.

A secreted extracellular endopeptidase that assembles on matrix-rich surfaces through fibronectin and kringle modules, then uses a trypsin-like catalytic core to execute tightly regulated proteolysis of secreted and pericellular substrates.
