It is synthesized and folded in the rough endoplasmic reticulum en route to secretion, where its adhesion domains concentrate the zymogen to control extracellular remodeling and signaling pathways characteristic of coagulation-like and growth factor–modulating cascades.

A soluble heme-dependent oxidoreductase in Agrobacterium that decomposes hydrogen peroxide via catalase–peroxidase chemistry and assembles through homotypic interactions to stabilize its active site. It operates primarily in the cytoplasm to buffer oxidative stress and is also secreted or retained at the cell envelope, where it shapes pericellular redox conditions during host interaction. By cycling its heme through high-valent intermediates, it removes peroxide and likely coordinates with secretion and matrix-binding systems to function both inside and outside the cell.

A surface-exposed, single-pass membrane adhesin in Mycoplasmoides gallisepticum that uses a large N-terminal ectodomain to mediate homotypic clustering and high-avidity binding at the cell surface. By assembling into a membrane-spanning adhesin–pore complex, it couples adhesion to formation of a conduit across the envelope and participates in secretion-linked envelope biogenesis. Its mechanism centers on homooligomerization of the adhesin scaffold to stabilize a pore-forming assembly that anchors in the membrane and projects an adhesive ectodomain outward.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator in Arabidopsis that uses a basic-leucine zipper module to bind promoter DNA and dimerize, thereby assembling transcriptional complexes that integrate abscisic acid, gibberellin, and sugar signals to control seed development and germination. By switching between activation and repression modes through its extended regulatory region, it modulates gene networks underlying seedling establishment and environmental stress responses, ultimately tuning transcriptional outputs that restrain or promote germination depending on hormonal and metabolic cues.

A plant multi-pass membrane channel that opens in response to mechanical and osmotic stress to conduct small cations, including calcium, thereby coupling membrane tension and water balance to intracellular signaling. It assembles a gated pore through a heptahelical core controlled by a cytosolic regulatory module and operates predominantly at the cell surface and intercellular junctions, with biosynthetic trafficking through the Golgi and occasional residence at the vacuole. By mediating stress-evoked cation influx, it helps coordinate ion fluxes that drive adaptive responses in Arabidopsis tissues.

A large cytoplasmic cytoskeletal scaffold that organizes actin–spectrin networks essential for epidermal–muscle attachment and body wall muscle development in C. elegans. It uses an N-terminal actin-binding head to anchor filaments, an extended spectrin-repeat rod to transmit and buffer mechanical forces, and a C-terminal WW–zinc-finger–EF-hand interaction hub that assembles calcium-tunable complexes. This multivalent architecture supports membrane-proximal cytoskeletal assemblies that drive myoblast fusion and stabilize epidermal–muscle junctions.

A soluble human serine/threonine kinase that assembles higher-order signaling complexes to coordinate antiviral and inflammatory responses. Its N-terminal catalytic core phosphorylates pathway nodes, while adjacent ubiquitin-like and coiled-coil modules scaffold assemblies that bind phosphorylated partners and route signals toward interferon and NF-κB pathways. Operating primarily in the cytosol and dynamically accumulating in the nucleoplasm, it promotes innate immune and inflammatory transcription, stimulates interferon production, and couples antiviral signaling to autophagy.

A soluble human lectin that uses a galectin-type β-sandwich fold to bind carbohydrates and assemble client proteins into higher-order complexes. It operates predominantly in the cytoplasm and also concentrates within nuclear matrix and nuclear bodies, where it scaffolds macromolecular assemblies. By organizing enzyme and glycoprotein partners, it manifests lysophospholipid-hydrolyzing activity and contributes to phospholipid metabolism, coupling glycan recognition and multivalent protein binding to regulate membrane-derived lipid pathways and nuclear structural hubs.

A soluble human GTPase that uses a P-loop NTPase core to bind and hydrolyze GTP, functioning as a nucleotide-tuned assembly factor that organizes protein complexes in the cytoplasm and at membrane-bounded organelles. By cycling between GTP- and GDP-bound states, it coordinates complex assembly and cargo delivery that underpin spermatid maturation and the structural organization of the nucleus, thereby coupling germ cell development to nuclear architecture.

A multi-pass cell-surface transporter that uses an MFS-like transmembrane core to move amphipathic organic anions and lipophilic mediators across the plasma membrane. An extracellular Kazal loop modulates substrate access and transport-coupled endocytosis, enabling efficient uptake and routing of prostaglandins and related lipidic anions. By controlling extracellular-to-intracellular flux of these mediators, the transporter promotes downstream kinase signaling and inflammatory transcriptional programs while residing stably in the plasma membrane.

A human F-box/LRR adaptor that assembles with SKP1–CUL1–RBX1 to form an SCF ubiquitin ligase and uses a curved leucine-rich repeat scaffold to capture substrates and regulatory enzymes. By docking to the SCF core and recruiting phosphatases and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase modules, it promotes substrate ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover while tuning autophagy and restraining inflammasome assembly. The complex operates primarily in the cytoplasm and can transiently associate with membranes where PI3K-driven signaling and inflammasome assembly are organized.

A single-pass cell-surface receptor that presents a large extracellular binding platform to capture ligands and organize receptor clusters, then signals through an intracellular tyrosine kinase core to autophosphorylate and recruit adaptor complexes. This architecture drives robust signal transduction and enhances MAP kinase pathway throughput. The ectodomain’s adhesive and calcium-tunable modules stabilize extracellular interactions, while the cytoplasmic kinase domain propagates intracellular signaling from the plasma membrane.

An extracellular glycoside hydrolase that trims β-linked glucans to remodel the fission yeast cell wall. By executing β-glucosidase chemistry at polarized growth sites and the division plane, it softens and reorganizes the glucan matrix to support wall biogenesis, organization, and mating-associated fusion. Its catalytic core drives hydrolysis of terminal β-glucosides, coordinating with wall-synthesizing and -restructuring systems at the mating projection tip and septum, and coupling to actin-guided delivery pathways that concentrate its activity where wall remodeling is required.

A soluble mitochondrial assembly factor that organizes ribonucleoprotein complexes for organellar protein synthesis. Its modular scaffold uses a central single-stranded nucleic-acid–binding core flanked by larger interaction domains to recruit and stabilize translation machinery and auxiliary biogenesis factors. By sustaining mitochondrial protein synthesis, it indirectly supports respiratory complex production and thereby maintains aerobic energy metabolism within the mitochondrial compartment.

A Golgi-localized, multi-pass membrane protein that couples an N-terminal inositol hexakisphosphate–sensing module to a C-terminal membrane module to coordinate phosphate-responsive signaling and transport. By binding inositol hexakisphosphate and allosterically tuning a membrane-embedded core, it maintains intracellular phosphate balance and shapes endomembrane trafficking pathways that feed into morphogenetic and receptor-mediated signaling circuits.

A stress-activated serine/threonine protein kinase that operates within a MAP kinase pathway to reprogram transcription and cytoskeletal effectors during environmental challenges. It becomes activated downstream of upstream kinases that sense heat shock, oxidative and osmotic stress, and then accumulates in the nucleus to phosphorylate transcriptional regulators. Through this signaling, it promotes stress tolerance and drives morphogenetic programs essential for filamentous growth and infection in the rice blast fungus.

A soluble archaeal enzyme that binds structured rRNA and tRNA and installs an aminocarboxypropyl group onto the small-subunit rRNA, thereby producing a hypermodification that tunes ribosome assembly and performance. Its N-terminal RNA/metal-binding module positions RNA substrates, while the C-terminal catalytic core executes aminocarboxypropyl transfer using SAM-coupled chemistry. Operating primarily in the cytoplasm but capable of associating with nucleoid-proximal RNA-processing hubs, it coordinates with ribosome biogenesis and tRNA-modification pathways to maintain RNA modification fidelity.

A membrane-anchored small GTPase switch that cycles between GTP- and GDP-bound states to control clathrin-mediated endocytosis, early endosome maturation, and multivesicular body sorting. By recruiting effectors in a nucleotide-dependent manner, it coordinates vesicle budding, cargo sorting, and membrane fusion. This trafficking hub shapes epithelial polarity and morphogenesis, supports germ cell and imaginal disc development, and sustains neuronal membrane remodeling underlying axon and dendrite growth, synaptic vesicle recycling, and synapse structure. It concentrates at the plasma membrane and early endosomes, with additional roles at the cortical cytoskeleton and within neuronal cell bodies and synapses.

A nuclear scaffold that assembles transcriptional and chromatin-regulatory complexes to stimulate gene expression and growth programs in fruit fly. Its N-terminal Kelch-repeat propeller builds multivalent interfaces that drive homotypic assembly and recruitment of co-regulators, while C-terminal immunoglobulin-like and fibronectin type III modules stabilize higher-order nuclear assemblies. By anchoring and modulating chromatin-remodeling and histone-modifying systems, it enhances transcriptional output and supports proliferative growth within the nucleus.

A soluble endonuclease that assembles a bipartite catalytic center to generate and coordinate loading of small regulatory RNAs. It uses an ATPase/helicase-like engine, a platform, and a PAZ anchor to measure and cleave double-stranded RNA into duplexes that seed silencing complexes. By binding partner proteins and coupling to small RNA pathways, it drives maturation of microRNA precursors and supports siRNA-mediated repression, thereby enforcing negative regulation of gene expression during embryonic development and tissue differentiation in the cytoplasm with transient nuclear involvement.

A nuclear serine/threonine kinase that assembles into higher-order kinase complexes to drive gene-regulatory programs. By binding ATP and catalyzing phosphorylation within a canonical kinase core, it activates transcriptional and chromatin-remodeling pathways that promote germline and neuronal differentiation. Its nuclear residency and assembly with transcriptional machinery enable promoter-proximal remodeling and positive control of RNA polymerase II–dependent transcription through targeted phosphorylation of nuclear substrates.

A nuclear chromatin-binding regulator that uses an N-terminal histone-tail engagement module and a C-terminal PHD finger to anchor on nucleosomes and read histone methylation states. By recruiting and stabilizing acetyltransferase and remodeling assemblies, it promotes acetylation-driven chromatin opening during DNA repair. This adaptor-like role positions it within acetyltransferase complexes and coordinates repair-coupled chromatin remodeling in the nucleus.

A nuclear chromatin reader that uses tandem Tudor domains to recognize methylated histone marks and anchor transcriptional coactivator assemblies at active promoters. By docking SAGA and ATAC complexes onto nucleosomes bearing methylated histone tails, it positions histone acetyltransferase and remodeling activities that loosen chromatin and promote transcriptional activation.

A cytoplasmic RNA-assembly scaffold that uses three tandem double-stranded RNA-binding modules to organize ribonucleoprotein complexes involved in post-transcriptional silencing. By stabilizing RNA-guided assemblies and recruiting partner proteins, it coordinates gene-regulatory circuits that shape embryonic and skeletal morphogenesis and supports oxidative-stress adaptation. Although non-enzymatic, it promotes phosphorylation-dependent signaling and can potentiate intrinsic apoptotic pathways by concentrating kinases and apoptotic regulators within higher-order assemblies.

A soluble scaffold of SCF-type ubiquitin ligase assemblies in mouse that organizes substrate-recognition modules at its N-terminus and catalyzes ubiquitin transfer through a neddylation-activated C-terminal core. By assembling with distinct receptor subunits, it directs both mono- and K48-linked ubiquitination to drive proteasome-dependent turnover of regulatory proteins. Operating prominently in the nucleoplasm, it shapes cell proliferation, morphogenesis, and apoptosis by coupling precise substrate capture to efficient ubiquitin signaling.

A small, soluble scaffold in Thermotoga maritima that forms homomeric assemblies to organize and stabilize biosynthetic machinery. By using a thiamine-binding-like fold to drive self-association, it likely nucleates higher-order complexes that enhance lysine pathway efficiency under thermophilic conditions. Its primary role is intracellular scaffolding, with occasional extracellular association possible through peripheral assemblies or non-classical export pathways.

A cytosolic bifunctional enzyme in Enterococcus that combines a soluble acyltransferase scaffold with a pyridoxal phosphate–dependent racemase core to coordinate amino acid chemistry with antibiotic assembly. The N-terminal acyltransferase fold supports acyl-group remodeling used during glycopeptide antibiotic biosynthesis, while the C-terminal racemase barrel mediates alanine stereoinversion to balance amino acid pools and potentially adjust stereochemistry on pathway intermediates. Together these activities channel flux into vancomycin-related pathways within the cytoplasm.

A multi-pass membrane cation channel in Arabidopsis that assembles as a tetramer and resides primarily at the plasma membrane, where osmotic and mechanical cues gate its pore to permit calcium-permeable conductance. A sizable cytosolic regulatory platform tunes opening and feedback, enabling controlled calcium influx that initiates and modulates cellular responses to osmotic and hyperosmotic stress. By coupling membrane-embedded conduction with cytosolic signal integration, it regulates calcium import and coordinates broader stress-adaptation pathways.

A nuclear assembly factor that uses an N-terminal ubiquitin-associated–like interaction module to homodimerize and recruit partners, coupled to a central nuclease/phosphatase fold that organizes chromatin-associated complexes. By tuning transcriptional machinery and DNA–protein cross-link responses, it dampens RNA polymerase II–driven gene expression during developmental programs and supports germline maintenance through regulated assembly and signaling rather than overt catalytic turnover.

A cytoplasmic adaptor that assembles calcium-regulated cytolinker complexes to stabilize actin-rich structures and the dystrophin-associated scaffold in Caenorhabditis elegans. By coupling an EF-hand calcium-sensing core to a ZZ-type interaction module, it binds cytoskeletal elements and organizes membrane-proximal assemblies that maintain sarcomere integrity, neuromuscular junction architecture, and cholinergic synaptic function. Through this scaffolding mechanism it supports muscle cell homeostasis and organismal locomotion by coordinating cytoskeletal and membrane-associated networks.

A secreted extracellular matrix scaffold that incorporates into basement membrane networks and pericellular fibrils. Its collagenous core forms a rigid rod that assembles matrix architecture, while a cysteine-rich tail stabilizes extracellular folds and promotes receptor and matrix binding. By organizing the extracellular environment at the plasma membrane and cell junctions, it modulates perisynaptic matrix structure and thereby influences neurotransmitter handling and cholinergic signaling.

A nucleolar assembly factor that organizes small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein complexes to guide site-specific modification and maturation of ribosomal RNA. It uses a conserved Nop scaffold to bind small nucleolar RNAs and recruit partner proteins and ATP-dependent remodelers, thereby coordinating rRNA processing with nucleolar transcription and RNA trafficking. The complex concentrates in nucleolar subcompartments and traffics through Cajal bodies, with soluble pools in the cytosol and transient associations that reflect dynamic assembly and sorting of ribonucleoprotein particles.

A mitochondrial matrix-associated assembly factor that organizes the coenzyme Q biosynthetic machinery. It forms a soluble scaffold that stabilizes and aligns pathway enzymes handling redox transformations and hydrophobic intermediates, thereby sustaining efficient production of ubiquinone for mitochondrial respiration. Its role is structural and organizational rather than directly catalytic, positioning the pathway at the matrix side of the organelle to coordinate assembly and flux through the ubiquinone pathway.

A cytosolic, PLP-dependent aminotransferase that functions as a homodimer to catalyze the terminal step of the serine biosynthetic pathway by transferring amino groups between phosphoserine and glutamate. Its class-V architecture organizes a PLP-binding pocket that cycles between internal and external aldimines to drive reversible transamination. By coupling nitrogen transfer to serine production, it integrates with broader amino acid and PLP metabolism in the cytosol and likely operates within transient multi-enzyme assemblies that optimize pathway flux.

A nuclear chromatin reader that uses a bromodomain module to recognize acetylated histone tails and a NET domain to assemble regulatory complexes that shape higher-order chromatin. By coupling histone mark recognition to the recruitment of remodeling and deacetylase machinery, it helps establish and maintain chromatin boundaries that confine heterochromatin and stabilize euchromatin within the nucleus.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in rat that uses the inward sodium gradient to drive concentrative uptake of dicarboxylates and related metabolites across the cell membrane. It mediates sodium-dependent transport of citrate, succinate, and fumarate, and can also translocate L‑aspartate and N‑acetyl‑L‑aspartate. By coupling Na+ binding to alternating-access conformational changes, it supplies central carbon intermediates and amino acids to cellular pathways, operating as a concentrative carrier at the membrane to support epithelial and renal solute handling.

A polytopic membrane protein in Arabidopsis that resides at the plasma membrane and functions as a surface-embedded organizer. Through multivalent protein binding, it assembles and restrains membrane complexes that produce cellulose, thereby dampening cellulose accumulation and tuning cell wall biosynthesis. Its multi-pass architecture provides interaction surfaces that modulate the assembly and activity of cellulose-producing machinery at membrane microdomains, producing a net negative regulation of cellulose output.

A cytoplasmic SAM-dependent methyltransferase that completes the 5′ cap maturation pathway by installing the N7-methyl group on the cap guanine of RNA. By binding S-adenosylmethionine and catalyzing guanine-N7 methylation, it stabilizes capped transcripts and promotes efficient translation. Its soluble architecture and participation in cytoplasmic RNA maturation hubs explain coordination with broader RNA modification and tRNA processing pathways, situating the enzyme as a central node that links cap formation to downstream RNA metabolism in Toxoplasma.

A nucleocytoplasmic scaffold that uses multivalent protein binding to organize polarity and spindle-orienting assemblies in nematode cells. By assembling cortical and microtubule-associated complexes, it positions and regulates meiotic and mitotic transitions, guides pronuclear migration, and establishes anterior–posterior polarity that feeds into early differentiation. Its soluble architecture concentrates in the cytoplasm with transient nuclear engagement, where it coordinates axis specification and spindle orientation through adaptor-mediated interactions rather than catalysis.

A junctional scaffold in the coccidian parasite that organizes adhesive complexes during schizogony. It concentrates at cell–cell interfaces between daughter schizonts, where it uses an extended adhesive module to assemble multiprotein assemblies that stabilize intercellular contacts and align membrane domains with cortical actin. By nucleating and reinforcing junctional architecture, it helps establish and maintain polarized cell morphology essential for daughter-cell adhesion and maturation.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in malaria parasites that mediates xenobiotic and thiol flux across endomembrane compartments. It likely uses an alternating-access mechanism to move chloroquine and related small molecules, and to shuttle glutathione between the biosynthetic route and the digestive vacuole. By energizing transport through proton gradients, it supports drug accumulation and redox-dependent heme detoxification, with maturation in the endoplasmic reticulum and steady-state residence at the food vacuole and vesicular pathways.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator in Fusarium verticillioides that uses a fungal zinc-cluster DNA-binding module to recognize specific promoter motifs and assemble co-regulatory complexes that elevate expression of the fumonisin biosynthetic machinery. By coupling precise DNA recognition with recruitment of transcriptional and chromatin-modifying activities, it drives the transcriptional program underlying secondary metabolite production and coordinates pathway timing and output.

A membrane-proximal guanine nucleotide exchange factor that uses a tripartite catalytic scaffold to activate Rab GTPases and thereby drive endocytic and signaling assemblies at the cytoplasmic face of membranes. A central exchange module catalyzes GDP release from Rab substrates, while an embedded lipid-binding module targets the complex to diacylglycerol-rich surfaces near the plasma membrane. By remodeling endosomal pathways and organizing signaling platforms, it enhances host inflammatory signaling cascades and contributes to host-pathway modulation during fungal–host interactions.

A ubiquitin-like autophagy factor that cycles between a soluble cytoplasmic state and a membrane-anchored state to drive autophagosome biogenesis. After proteolytic priming, it becomes conjugated to phosphatidylethanolamine and accumulates on autophagic membranes, where it scaffolds effector assemblies that expand and seal the isolation membrane. By organizing selective autophagy pathways, it supports assembly of autophagosomes and contributes to cellular programs that neutralize intracellular threats, including antifungal defenses.

A secreted human enzyme with a sulfatase-like catalytic core that hydrolyzes extracellular sulfate esters. By editing sulfated macromolecules in the pericellular space, it contributes to sulfur compound turnover and shapes tissue-level signaling and matrix remodeling that influence development and host defense. Its alkaline-phosphatase-like fold and conserved catalytic site support metal-assisted hydrolysis outside the cell, positioning the enzyme to modulate extracellular pathways linked to antibiotic responsiveness.

A calcium- and diacylglycerol-gated serine/threonine kinase that translocates from the cytoplasm to membranes and signaling assemblies where it phosphorylates substrates controlling apoptosis and gene expression. Its N-terminal calcium/lipid-sensing modules drive membrane recruitment, while a C-terminal AGC kinase core executes phosphorylation and autophosphorylation. By assembling at immune synapses and other signaling membranes and shuttling to the nucleus, it integrates cAMP-linked pathways, modulates translational capacity in the cytoplasm, and orchestrates context-dependent apoptotic and transcriptional programs.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator in fruit fly that uses an N-terminal DNA-binding module to anchor at enhancers and promoters and a C-terminal co-regulator–recruitment region to assemble transcriptional activation complexes. By organizing co-activators and chromatin-modifying assemblies, it elevates gene expression programs governed by enhancer logic and developmental signaling within nuclear transcription regulator assemblies.

A soluble quorum-sensing transcriptional activator in Pseudomonas aeruginosa that binds acyl-homoserine lactone signals to dimerize and engage promoter DNA, thereby elevating transcription of operons that drive biofilm formation and virulence. By coupling signal perception to DNA binding and RNA polymerase recruitment, it coordinates programs that enhance protease secretion and lipid biosynthesis within the cytoplasm and nucleoid-associated transcriptional assemblies.

A ubiquitin-like, membrane-anchored scaffold that orchestrates autophagosome biogenesis and selective autophagy in rat cells. By undergoing C-terminal processing and conjugation to phosphatidylethanolamine, it transitions from a soluble cytosolic state to a membrane-tethered form that organizes autophagic membranes. This reversible lipidation anchors and stabilizes autophagosomal rims, recruits cargo-selective adaptors and effectors through multivalent binding, and supports pathways that clear damaged organelles and pathogen-associated material. Its trafficking and assembly roles position it at autophagosome membranes and associated cytoplasmic vesicles, with transient residence at the Golgi apparatus and cytoplasm.

A human diacylglycerol-activated serine/threonine kinase that assembles at membrane microdomains via N‑terminal lipid-targeting modules and uses a C‑terminal catalytic core to phosphorylate substrates controlling receptor internalization and cytoskeletal remodeling. By coupling membrane recruitment to catalytic output, it orchestrates endocytic uptake and signal transduction at specialized cell–cell interfaces such as the immunological synapse.

A multi-pass plasma membrane transporter that forms a high-affinity, sodium-independent pathway for essential neutral and cationic amino acids. It assembles into a surface complex that concentrates branched-chain substrates such as leucine and supports exchange of multiple amino acids, thereby sustaining intracellular pools used for anabolic metabolism and nutrient-responsive signaling. Its alternating-access mechanism arises from a membrane-embedded transporter core that confers selective uptake and broad substrate range at the cell surface.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in rabbit that assembles a heteromeric high-affinity pathway for neutral amino acid uptake at the apical surface of epithelial cells. It concentrates leucine and phenylalanine and other neutral amino acids by alternating-access translocation, thereby driving reabsorption and maintaining systemic amino acid balance. The complex resides at the plasma membrane—particularly the apical membrane of renal epithelia—where it operates as part of a membrane protein assembly that stabilizes folding, trafficking, and high-affinity transport.

A multi-pass membrane transporter in mouse that assembles at the cell surface to mediate sodium-independent and sodium-dependent exchange of L-amino acids, with a preference for neutral and cationic substrates including phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan. By cycling through an alternating-access mechanism embedded in a membrane pore, it concentrates and releases amino acids to tune intracellular pools that feed anabolic and signaling pathways. The complex operates at the plasma membrane, where an accessory glycoprotein partner stabilizes and regulates its activity and surface residency.

A secreted four-helix bundle cytokine that signals in the extracellular milieu to modulate immune and epithelial pathways. By presenting a conserved receptor-binding surface, it assembles receptor complexes that activate JAK–STAT signaling, thereby tuning cellular programs engaged during cold exposure and other stresses. Its soluble nature and cytokine architecture position it as an extracellular modulator that coordinates tissue and immune responses through receptor-mediated signaling.

A secreted human cytokine that adopts a four-helix bundle to bind cell-surface receptor complexes and trigger signaling that tempers immune cytotoxicity and supports endothelial survival. By engaging its cognate receptor system in the extracellular space, it initiates pathways that dampen complement-driven cell damage and reduce apoptosis in endothelial cells, consistent with a soluble mediator that operates through receptor-mediated signaling rather than enzymatic activity.

A signal-activated transcriptional regulator that shuttles between cytoplasm and nucleus to couple cytokine and growth factor inputs to gene expression programs controlling proliferation and differentiation. It assembles via N-terminal and coiled-coil modules, binds DNA through a central recognition core, and uses a C-terminal phosphotyrosine-recognition unit to dimerize and become transcriptionally active after receptor-proximal phosphorylation. This architecture enables stimulus-dependent nuclear entry and activation of target genes downstream of pathways such as leukemia inhibitory factor signaling, with transient association to membrane-proximal receptor complexes preceding nuclear transcriptional control.

A secreted cytokine that adopts a four-helix bundle to act as an extracellular ligand, engaging a class I cytokine receptor complex to trigger JAK–STAT signaling. Through this pathway it promotes epithelial cell proliferation and suppresses apoptosis, while coordinating immune responses and tissue repair characteristic of IL-13-type cytokines.

A signal-activated transcriptional regulator that shuttles between cytoplasm and nucleus. It remains cytoplasmic in a latent state and, upon tyrosine phosphorylation downstream of cytokine and growth-factor pathways, dimerizes through a phosphotyrosine-recognition module and accumulates in the nucleus. There it binds specific promoter elements and recruits co-regulators to drive gene expression programs that implement responses to cytokines such as leukemia inhibitory factor.

A soluble intracellular metalloaminopeptidase in fruit fly that assembles via an N-terminal regulatory module and uses a C-terminal catalytic core to remove N-terminal residues—particularly proline and leucine—from short oligopeptides. By trimming N-termini in the nucleus, it contributes to intracellular peptide turnover and amino acid recycling, thereby supporting nuclear proteostasis and broader proteolysis pathways.

A cytosolic enzyme that introduces a hydroxyl group at the 9-position of medium-to-long-chain fatty acid precursors, thereby generating 9-hydroxymyristate and channeling flux into hydroxylated fatty acid end products. Its alpha/beta hydrolase scaffold forms and resolves acyl-enzyme intermediates that enable controlled monooxygenation chemistry within the fatty acid biosynthetic network, coordinating with cytosolic elongation and tailoring systems to steer saturated and unsaturated lipid pathways.

A multi-pass membrane component of a type VII secretion apparatus in Staphylococcus aureus that oligomerizes to form a secretion conduit in the cell membrane. By assembling a permease-like pore that exports surface adhesins and other pilin-like substrates, it promotes accumulation of host-binding factors at the bacterial surface and thereby supports adhesion during colonization.

A soluble fungal terpene-forming enzyme that operates in the cytosol to sculpt a GGPP-derived intermediate en route to a macrocyclic diterpenoid mycotoxin. Its isoprenoid-synthase-like catalytic core organizes Mg2+-dependent chemistry that drives carbocation-mediated rearrangements, channeling flux from the mevalonate pathway into specialized diterpenoid assembly. The product is subsequently refined by cytochrome P450s and an acetyltransferase within a dedicated biosynthetic gene cluster that culminates in a complex macrocyclic scaffold.

A soluble phage-encoded host-modulatory effector that extends the intracellular life cycle by preventing premature host cell death. It operates through multivalent protein binding rather than catalysis, assembling transient complexes in the bacterial cytoplasm and concentrating into nuclear foci that likely tune nucleocytoplasmic trafficking and survival pathways. By suppressing host apoptosis and stabilizing cellular homeostasis, it safeguards the cellular environment required for efficient phage propagation.

A DNA-binding architectural protein in a staphylococcal phage that organizes and compacts the viral genome to drive rolling-circle replication and subsequently supports capsid morphogenesis. By forming nucleoprotein assemblies that stabilize replication intermediates, it promotes strand displacement and efficient genome amplification. Its structural role extends to the assembly environment of the procapsid, where it helps template higher-order lattice formation essential for building the mature virion.

A soluble lyase in the corn smut fungus that catalyzes fumarate-elimination chemistry on two adenylate intermediates to sustain purine biosynthesis. It converts N6-(1,2-dihydroxyethyl)AMP to AMP and ADP and also transforms N-succinyladenine to AMP and fumarate. By regenerating AMP and clearing reactive succinylated adenylates, it stabilizes nucleotide flux that feeds into IMP formation. The enzyme likely operates as a soluble oligomer associated with mitochondria, where purine synthesis and adenylate balance are coordinated through energy-coupled metabolons.

A Golgi-resident, single-pass type II membrane glycosyltransferase that installs terminal fucose via an alpha-(1→3) linkage onto type 1 and type 2 glycan termini, thereby shaping Lewis-type and ABO-like epitopes during protein glycosylation. Its luminal catalytic domain uses a GT10 fold to bind GDP-fucose and transfer fucose with bifunctional specificity, operating within medial Golgi cisternae to finalize glycan repertoires that modulate adhesion and signaling in the secretory pathway.

A secreted fungal endoglucanase that hydrolyzes internal β-1,4 linkages of cellulose and related glucans outside the cell. By fragmenting insoluble plant cell wall polymers into soluble dextrins, it fuels saccharification pathways and supports nutrient acquisition and host–pathogen interface remodeling. Its extracellular action is driven by a metal-assisted catalytic core that binds and cleaves cellulose within the secretory pathway’s output, coordinating with other surface-associated enzymes to accelerate cellulose breakdown.

An endoplasmic reticulum–associated cytochrome P450 monooxygenase in montbretia that tailors diterpenoid intermediates en route to montbrettin A. Anchored to the ER membrane and equipped with a heme-dependent catalytic center, it uses electrons from cellular redox systems to activate molecular oxygen and introduce precise oxidative modifications that drive flux through the specialized diterpenoid pathway.

A Golgi-resident, single-pass type II membrane glycosyltransferase that installs terminal fucose onto maturing glycans using GDP-fucose, thereby generating fucosylated epitopes central to glycan biosynthesis and cellular recognition. Its luminal catalytic domain transfers fucose in an alpha configuration to suitable acceptors, producing both alpha-1,3 and alpha-1,4 linkages observed in vitro and supporting assembly of complex glycoconjugates within the medial Golgi cisternae.

A medial-Golgi, type II membrane-anchored fucosyltransferase that uses a nucleotide-sugar–binding catalytic ectodomain to install fucose in an alpha-(1→3) linkage onto terminal and internal hydroxyls of maturing glycans. By transferring fucose from GDP-fucose onto N-acetylneuraminic acid and N-acetylglucosamine acceptors, it builds fucosylated epitopes within the Golgi pathway and supports broader glycan assembly. Its single-pass topology positions the catalytic domain in the Golgi lumen, where it collaborates with neighboring glycosylation machinery to finalize carbohydrate biosynthesis.

A soluble copper-dependent amine oxidase in Indian heliotrope that catalyzes oxidative deamination of primary amines, including L-amino acids and polyamines, generating aldehydes and ammonia while using molecular oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor. By reshaping intracellular amine and aldehyde pools, it tunes cellular programs that respond to nitrogenous metabolites and salt stress. The enzyme is predominantly cytosolic but likely engages with wall- and spore-associated compartments in development and dormancy, where amine turnover and aldehyde chemistry influence matrix organization and germination.

A cytoplasmic viral replicase that powers DNA synthesis by coupling ATP-driven conformational cycling to nucleotide-handling chemistry. It operates a bidirectional strand-displacement replication program, using ATP hydrolysis to fuel template cleavage and nucleotide transfer steps that sustain processive DNA synthesis and directional switching within cytoplasmic replication factories.

A stonyfish-derived cytolytic defense factor that assembles via homotypic interactions into membrane-perforating complexes. Its N-terminal pore-forming core and associated helical/thioredoxin-like modules drive oligomerization and membrane engagement, while a C-terminal SPRY interaction hub tunes target recognition. This architecture enables cytolysis that supports antiviral and antisymbiotic defense. The protein operates primarily in the cytoplasm, with a functional pool in the nucleus that likely reflects regulated assembly and targeting during immune surveillance.

A secreted cytolytic toxin from reef stonefish that assembles into higher-order complexes to perforate target membranes. An N-terminal fusogenic core drives membrane attack, a central helical and thioredoxin-like scaffold stabilize oligomerization, and a C-terminal β-sandwich platform promotes self-association and adaptor capture. This architecture enables rapid pore formation that eliminates susceptible cells and indirectly enhances host defense against symbionts and viruses. The protein is soluble and secreted, acting extracellularly before docking onto target membranes, with transient intracellular assembly phases.

A soluble decarboxylase that generates quinolinic acid by removing CO2 from a hydroxy- and carboxylated imidazoline intermediate. This reaction supplies a key metabolite that supports pathways connected to aromatic amino acid metabolism and cofactor formation. The enzyme operates as a cofactor-independent carboxy-lyase and dynamically partitions between cytoplasm, peroxisomes, and the mitochondrial matrix, where it likely couples quinolinic acid production to local demands of NAD-dependent metabolism.

A soluble cytoplasmic metalloaminopeptidase that assembles into a homomeric ring to remove N-terminal residues from intracellular peptides, thereby sustaining amino acid recycling and peptide homeostasis. Its oligomeric assembly and cytoplasmic residency position it to modulate proteostasis pathways that feed into developmental programs, including mesodermal patterning. Dynamic association with organelle-rich cytoplasm likely supports its role in peptide turnover and signaling.

A cytoplasmic HECT-type ubiquitin ligase that uses an N-terminal membrane/cytoskeleton-targeting module and central WW repeats to recruit PY-motif-bearing substrates and adaptors, then employs a C-terminal catalytic center to transfer ubiquitin and drive proteasome-directed turnover. By assembling transient homo-oligomeric complexes and operating at cytosolic and membrane-proximal sites, it remodels signaling and cytoskeletal networks through ubiquitin-dependent degradation pathways.

A modular scaffold that uses an N-terminal MYND zinc finger and an extended helical repeat array to assemble higher-order complexes. By combining selective partner recognition with multivalent helical scaffolding, it promotes trimer formation and organizes cargo–motor assemblies associated with microtubule-based transport. This architecture supports a role in cytosolic kinesin-associated assemblies that coordinate cargo loading and directional trafficking.

A soluble CBS-repeat scaffold in Pyrobaculum calidifontis that organizes macromolecular assemblies at the transcriptional hub. Its tandem CBS modules create multivalent binding surfaces that assemble and regulate protein complexes involved in RNA biogenesis. By docking onto the transcription machinery and associated RNA-handling factors, it coordinates transcription with mRNA maturation through ligand-responsive, noncatalytic interactions that fine-tune assembly and handoff of nascent transcripts.

A human multi-pass membrane transporter–scaffold that resides predominantly at the cell surface and traffics through endosomal and Golgi membranes. Its EamA/EmrE-type core supports translocation of small metabolites, while the solute-carrier family envelope promotes assembly with regulatory partners. Together these features enable binding-driven control of transport pathways that handle organic cations and thiamine, with dynamic cycling between the plasma membrane and intracellular organelles and occasional perinuclear/nuclear associations that coordinate membrane trafficking with metabolite availability.

A soluble cytoplasmic enzyme that installs and extends glutamate side chains on tubulin, thereby tuning microtubule behavior during cell division. By catalyzing ATP-dependent polyglutamylation of tubulin—preferentially on the alpha subunit—it shapes spindle-associated microtubules to support accurate mitosis. The enzyme operates in the cytoplasm and concentrates at the spindle, where its modification activity coordinates with other tubulin-modifying systems to regulate spindle assembly and stability.

A secreted, high-molecular-weight surface adhesin in Flavobacterium johnsoniae that assembles into oligomeric arrays to mediate firm attachment to host-associated surfaces. By building a multivalent scaffold, it concentrates binding sites that secure bacterium-to-host contacts, promoting stable colonization and nutrient access. Its adhesive architecture supports tight association with host cell surfaces and soluble pools that interface with host cytoplasm during symbiotic interactions.

A soluble cytoplasmic enzyme that installs glutamate side chains on target proteins, with a primary role in decorating tubulin tails to regulate microtubule behavior. It uses ATP-dependent ligation chemistry to polyglutamylate substrates, showing strong preference for α-tubulin over β-tubulin and acting on soluble targets including matrix-associated proteins. By tuning the polyglutamylation state of cytoplasmic assemblies, it modulates interactions with motors and microtubule-associated factors and thereby influences cytoskeletal dynamics and associated trafficking pathways.

A membrane-associated metalloprotease in Klebsiella pneumoniae that anchors at the inner membrane and uses a metalloprotease core to cleave misfolded or stalled membrane-associated proteins during stress. By assembling transient recognition complexes and executing proteolytic quality control, it helps the cell recover from heat, hypotonic, and UV challenges. Its soluble catalytic domain is positioned at the membrane interface, where it engages substrates through specific protein–protein contacts and contributes to membrane-proximal proteostasis.

A soluble peroxisomal enzyme that catalyzes the condensation of glyoxylate with acetyl-CoA to form malate and CoA, thereby driving the glyoxylate shunt that sustains carbon flow when complete glycolysis is bypassed. Its catalytic core is a TIM-barrel that organizes metal-assisted chemistry, while flanking domains stabilize the active site and mediate transient assemblies with pathway partners. By operating in the peroxisome, it couples to lipid-derived acetyl-CoA and glyoxylate handling, supporting anaplerotic balance and detoxification through malate production.

A cytoplasmic, endosome-associated scaffold that assembles the WASH core complex to coordinate endosomal trafficking with actin remodeling. By recruiting and activating actin-nucleating machinery at endosomal membranes, it drives branched actin assembly that powers endocytic recycling and retrograde transport toward the Golgi. This coupling of membrane sorting to cytoskeletal dynamics supports exocytic routes and influences protrusive behaviors and matrix remodeling through regulated actin nucleation and organization.

A soluble mitochondrial-matrix enzyme that combines an N-terminal dethiobiotin-synthase–like module with a C-terminal pyridoxal phosphate–dependent aminotransferase core to drive transamination chemistry that sustains biotin production. By assembling a pathway-proximal scaffold with a catalytically competent PLP fold, it channels nitrogen into biotin biosynthesis within the organelle. Its soluble architecture and matrix localization indicate a role in coordinating nitrogen flow and intermediate transfer rather than general amino acid metabolism, thereby supporting biotin-dependent mitochondrial functions.

A soluble cytoplasmic enzyme in Streptomyces that employs a hotdog-fold catalytic core to perform oxygen-dependent tailoring chemistry on fatty acid–derived intermediates. By organizing oxidative steps that sculpt and cyclize acyl-derived scaffolds, it contributes to the maturation of specialized small molecules that branch from central fatty acid pathways. Its soluble architecture and pathway context indicate a dimeric oxidoreductase that collaborates with acyl carrier and acyl-CoA systems to channel intermediates toward secondary metabolite assembly.

A membrane-associated scaffold that self-assembles into homotrimers and higher-order arrays to organize supramolecular complexes at the cell surface of Porphyromonas gingivalis. Its N-terminal module nucleates oligomerization, while a central beta-propeller core provides a rigid platform for multivalent contacts, thereby stabilizing and positioning surface assemblies such as adhesins and secretion/pilus structures at the membrane interface.

An outer-membrane assembly factor in Porphyromonas gingivalis that uses a periplasmic scaffold to capture and guide β-barrel precursors toward insertion and folding in the bacterial outer membrane. By orchestrating outer-membrane biogenesis, it stabilizes the cell envelope and indirectly supports virulence pathways that remodel host membranes and promote release of virus-like particles. Its mechanism relies on multivalent binding to substrates and periplasmic chaperones, coupled to a membrane-embedded assembly core that transiently conducts unfolded substrates to mature outer-membrane proteins.

An outer-membrane-associated folding catalyst in Porphyromonas gingivalis that accelerates the maturation of periplasmic and surface-exposed proteins by catalyzing proline isomerization. Its soluble catalytic core promotes efficient acquisition of native structure for factors destined for or operating at the cell surface, thereby supporting envelope protein biogenesis and robustness of the outer membrane. The enzyme likely acts near outer-membrane assembly hubs, transiently engaging secreted adhesins and proteases to prevent folding bottlenecks at the membrane interface.

An outer-membrane biogenesis scaffold in Porphyromonas gingivalis that organizes and stabilizes assemblies required for outer-membrane protein formation. Its helical-repeat solenoid creates a multivalent binding platform that promotes homotypic oligomerization and recruits partner subunits and substrates to drive outer-membrane complex assembly. Operating adjacent to and coordinated with pore-forming pathways, it likely binds and organizes client β-barrel precursors and assembly modules to ensure efficient maturation and insertion.

A multi-pass membrane adhesin in Porphyromonas gingivalis that integrates host-cell attachment with membrane transport. It mediates binding to human gingival cells and fibronectin, using a membrane-embedded scaffold to capture host ligands and couple them to an ATP-driven transporter assembly. By stabilizing interactions within a larger complex, it promotes firm adhesion at the host–pathogen interface while coordinating uptake and envelope-associated processes at the cell surface.

A secreted fungal serine endopeptidase that is produced as an autoinhibited zymogen and activated outside the cell to remodel extracellular proteins. After removal of its inhibitory propeptide, the enzyme employs a catalytic triad to cleave internal peptide bonds with broad substrate tolerance, supporting extracellular proteolysis and nutrient acquisition. Its surface chemistry also engages human immunoglobulins, positioning immunoglobulins as substrates or modulators that fine-tune activity in the extracellular environment.

A soluble SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase in Aspergillus flavus that installs a methyl group onto a hydroxylated intermediate within the aflatoxin assembly line. By using a winged-helix-like scaffold to position substrates and a C-terminal catalytic core to transfer the methyl group from SAM, it fine-tunes the electronic properties of pathway intermediates and channels flux toward aflatoxin scaffolds. Operating as part of the aflatoxin biosynthetic ensemble, it contributes to the production of aflatoxins B and G series—secondary metabolites central to mycotoxin formation—and functions predominantly in the cytoplasm through transient metabolon assemblies.

A nuclear DNA recombinase in the malaria parasite that uses a core-binding module to target chromosomal repeat sites and a tyrosine-recombinase catalytic core to cleave and rejoin DNA strands. By executing precise strand exchange, it remodels terminal repeats and stabilizes transposition-derived sequences, thereby supporting genome defense and adaptive recombination pathways within the nucleus.

A secreted peptide hormone produced by a parasitic wasp that acts in the extracellular milieu to reprogram physiology of target insects. By engaging cell-surface receptors and triggering systemic signaling, it modulates neuronal and immune pathways that influence how hosts cope with microbes, thereby intersecting with antibacterial defenses against Gram-negative bacteria. Its mechanism is consistent with a processed, secreted signaling molecule that binds extracellular targets to elicit endocrine and paracrine responses.

A secreted venom allergen from central American paper wasp that adopts a cysteine-rich secretory protein–type fold to act as an extracellular effector. Its stabilized binding surface enables high-affinity interactions with extracellular targets, supporting a role in organismal defense by modulating membrane-associated signaling and cytoskeletal control during envenomation. Operating outside the cell, it contributes to defensive strategies by assembling transient complexes that suppress prey and parasite responses.

A secreted venom-derived inhibitory peptide that suppresses calcium entry by binding and inhibiting voltage-gated calcium channels at the extracellular membrane surface. It potently blocks L-type channels and weakly affects T-type channels, with a broader tendency to inhibit potassium, TRP, and T-type calcium conductances. By stabilizing non-conducting channel states, it dampens excitability and contractility in prey, acting through an extracellular inhibitory interface characteristic of soluble venom peptides.

A soluble cytoplasmic electron-transfer enzyme that binds FAD and carries a 2Fe–2S center to funnel reducing power from pyridine nucleotides into a multicomponent monooxygenase system. By loading electrons onto its flavin core and buffering them through an iron–sulfur carrier, it supplies the reducing equivalents that drive oxygenase chemistry and supports cellular iron–sulfur cofactor handling. This reductase/transfer hub underpins catabolic redox pathways in hydrocarbon and aromatic compound metabolism by coupling NAD(P)H utilization to downstream oxygen insertion chemistry.

A large RNA-targeting effector from a spirochetal bacterium that assembles a soluble ribonucleoprotein complex to regulate gene expression and stress responses. Its fold creates extensive interfaces for guide RNA and partner proteins, enabling endonucleolytic control of transcripts that shape motility programs. The complex operates primarily in the cytoplasm with transient enrichment near nucleoid-associated transcription sites. A moonlighting metabolic facet consistent with chorismate mutase chemistry may couple central metabolism to RNA-target selection, thereby tuning pathways that drive swarming behavior.

A secreted extracellular metalloprotease that assembles a cysteine-rich, spacer- and thrombospondin-repeat scaffold to anchor within collagen-rich matrices and execute zinc-dependent proteolysis. By engaging extracellular matrix substrates and cell-surface adhesion systems, it remodels fibrinogen- and collagen-containing niches, thereby tuning adhesion and signaling pathways that dampen platelet aggregation and broader inter-organismal processes at vascular interfaces.

A Golgi-associated cytosolic scaffold that oligomerizes into higher-order assemblies to organize membrane-trafficking and ion-handling modules. By forming homotetrameric platforms, it recruits trafficking factors and stabilizes cation-transport assemblies at the Golgi–endosomal interface, thereby tuning secretory pathway dynamics and indirectly promoting cation movement across Golgi-related membranes.

A soluble copper-handling factor that uses a superoxide dismutase-like fold to transiently coordinate copper and zinc, forming a dimeric platform that loads copper onto apo-superoxide dismutases. By supplying essential copper to antioxidant enzymes, it sustains cellular defenses against oxidative stress and operates prominently at peroxisomes—sites of intense redox metabolism—thereby reinforcing peroxisomal antioxidant capacity through targeted metallochaperone activity.

A soluble bacterial nuclease-helicase that serves as the execution arm of adaptive immunity. It binds and unwinds single-stranded nucleic acids using an ATP-driven motor and then degrades the exposed strand via a metal-dependent nuclease center. This coupling of unwinding and degradation enables efficient dismantling of invasive nucleic acids during defense against phages and plasmids. The enzyme operates in the cytoplasm adjacent to the nucleoid, where it receives target substrates from guide-RNA–directed assemblies and carries out processive DNA breakdown.

A secreted endo-acting cellulase from a thermophilic saprotroph that hydrolyzes internal β-1,4 linkages of cellulose and related β-glucans, initiating saccharification of plant cell wall material outside the cell. Its GH45 catalytic core generates soluble oligosaccharides that feed downstream pathways, and its extracellular deployment positions it to act in concert with other carbohydrate-active enzymes to drive cellulose breakdown and channel released sugars into fungal metabolism.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator that uses a TALE-class homeobox core together with zinc finger and helix–turn–helix modules to bind DNA and assemble multiprotein regulatory complexes. By recruiting cofactors and engaging chromatin, it modulates RNA polymerase II transcription programs central to filamentous growth and host–pathogen gene networks in a nuclear environment.

A plasma-membrane–anchored syntaxin that organizes vesicle docking and fusion in a filamentous fungus. Its N-terminal regulatory module autoinhibits the C-terminal SNARE motif until licensed by trafficking cues, after which assembly of a SNARE complex drives bilayer merger. By coupling regulated protein–protein interactions to membrane fusion, it sustains vesicle-mediated transport and secretion at the cell surface.

A nuclear transcriptional activator that binds specific promoter sequences to elevate expression of a central regulator of extracellular carbohydrate utilization. By assembling coactivator and chromatin-remodeling machinery at target promoters, it drives a regulon that includes a master switch for plant cell wall–derived nutrient pathways. Its internal regulatory module tunes activity in response to carbohydrate-linked signals, enabling precise, signal-responsive activation of gene networks that support nutrient acquisition and downstream cell wall degradation programs.

A single-pass membrane-anchored scaffold in the fungal cell envelope that uses an extracellular mannoprotein-like module to engage and organize assemblies at the cell wall while a cytosolic C-terminal region drives homooligomerization and recruits ubiquitin-sensitive partners. By coupling extracellular wall association with intracellular multivalent binding, it coordinates membrane trafficking and wall-associated complexes at the membrane–cell wall interface to support polarized assembly and remodeling.

A nuclear regulatory scaffold in the plant-pathogenic fungus that assembles transcriptional and RNA-regulatory complexes to control gene expression programs linked to pathogenicity. It uses a multivalent interaction core to recruit proline-rich partners and a zinc finger module to stabilize nucleic acid-engaged assemblies, thereby modulating transcriptional outputs central to host interaction and virulence.

A soluble FAD-dependent oxidoreductase that operates within a fungal secondary-metabolite pathway assembling a complex mycotoxin. Its N-terminal FAD-oxidase core and C-terminal berberine-like module cooperate to abstract electrons from alcohol-bearing intermediates and drive oxidative steps that precede epoxide rearrangement and ring-forming chemistry. Acting within a biosynthetic ensemble that builds and modifies a tetraketide-derived scaffold, it likely functions in concert with pathway enzymes to channel reactive intermediates toward toxin formation and extracellular deployment.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator in the plant-pathogenic fungus Verticillium dahliae that combines a cupin-barrel scaffold with a C-terminal homeodomain to control gene expression during infection. The N-terminal cupin module likely senses cellular cues and stabilizes assemblies, while the homeodomain anchors the complex to chromatin to modulate transcriptional programs that drive virulence. By assembling multiprotein nuclear complexes, it fine-tunes host-interactive pathways that alter host cellular architecture and intersect with virus-modulated host gene expression.

A secreted fungal effector that accumulates at the cell wall–apoplast interface and promotes host colonization by degrading plant cell wall polysaccharides. It binds calcium and employs a composite mechanism that couples redox chemistry with hydrolysis to attack cellulose and mixed β-glucans, thereby initiating extracellular matrix breakdown and nutrient release during infection.

A secreted fungal aspartic endopeptidase that operates in the extracellular space to drive proteolysis and protein processing during host interaction. By using a pepsin-like catalytic core, it activates and remodels extracellular substrates, contributing to entry into host tissues and broader host-associated processes. Its activity likely proceeds via zymogen activation and broad substrate cleavage in the apoplast, supporting colonization and nutrient acquisition.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator in the filamentous pathogen Verticillium dahliae that uses a TALE-class homeodomain together with a C2H2 zinc finger array to bind promoter DNA and assemble regulatory complexes. By scaffolding partner proteins and coupling them to RNA polymerase II machinery, it modulates gene-expression programs that drive filamentous growth and infection. Its soluble, chromatin-associated architecture positions it in the nucleus during host interaction, where it coordinates transcriptional circuits central to pathogenic development.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator in the filamentous pathogen Verticillium dahliae that uses a TALE-class homeodomain together with C2H2 zinc-finger modules to assemble promoter-bound complexes and control gene expression. By organizing multivalent protein interactions on chromatin, it modulates transcriptional programs that impinge on sphingolipid biosynthesis, thereby tuning membrane and stress-response pathways essential for fungal development and host interaction.

An oxidoreductase in the carotenoid/anthocyanin-forming branch of secondary metabolism that catalyzes an oxidative step converting the colorless intermediate geodenumol toward the anthocyanin-like geodhenone. By installing oxidation that extends conjugation and stabilizes pigment-forming scaffolds, it drives flux through the geodenumol A pathway and promotes pigment and tetraterpenoid accumulation near the fungal cell periphery. Its activity likely occurs within a wall-proximal metabolon that channels hydrophobic intermediates toward deposition and stabilization.

A secreted fungal effector that operates outside host cells to dampen early innate immune responses. Its single isochorismatase-like hydrolase core suggests an extracellular hydrolytic enzyme that remodels ether-containing small molecules near the plant cell surface. By consuming or altering immune-promoting metabolites and thereby tuning receptor-initiated signaling, it suppresses host defense activation during infection.

A nuclear velvet-domain regulator in Verticillium dahliae that assembles transcriptional complexes to control developmental and stress-responsive gene expression. By forming a multivalent scaffold that binds other nuclear regulators and chromatin-modifying assemblies, it modulates transcriptional programs central to fungal development and pathogenicity. Its soluble nuclear architecture positions it to coordinate transcriptional machinery and chromatin, thereby tuning gene expression outputs in response to environmental cues.

A secreted serine endopeptidase from the Verticillium wilt fungus that operates outside the cell to cleave internal peptide bonds in a wide range of protein substrates. Its chymotrypsin-like fold and catalytic triad drive broad endoproteolysis, enabling efficient degradation of diverse extracellular targets such as casein, lipoproteins, and precursor toxins. By executing extracellular proteolysis, it contributes to nutrient acquisition and host interaction, likely after zymogen activation and stabilization by its conserved protease scaffold.

A Ras-association–targeted serine/threonine kinase that functions at the top of a MAP kinase cascade controlling cytokinesis and polarized growth in filamentous fungi. By docking to small GTPase-rich assemblies, it localizes to the hyphal apex and division sites, where it phosphorylates downstream kinases to drive septum formation and morphogenesis. Its N-terminal targeting module positions the catalytic core at membrane-proximal and nuclear-envelope–adjacent zones, coordinating spatially restricted signaling that couples septation with tip-directed growth.

A secreted subtilisin-like serine endopeptidase that is produced as a latent zymogen and activated outside the cell to drive broad-spectrum extracellular proteolysis. After removal of its inhibitory propeptide, the enzyme employs a classic catalytic triad to hydrolyze diverse protein substrates, supporting nutrient acquisition and remodeling of extracellular protein assemblies in the environment of the fungus.

A secreted fungal serine endopeptidase that operates outside the cell to degrade diverse extracellular proteins. Its subtilisin-like catalytic core forms a triad that drives peptide-bond hydrolysis and efficiently cleaves casein-like substrates and gelatin while sparing insulin A chain, indicating a preference for unfolded or flexible regions. By executing broad-spectrum extracellular proteolysis, it supports nutrient acquisition and virulence-associated remodeling in the extracellular milieu, likely after zymogen activation within its catalytic fold.

A secreted glycoside hydrolase that operates outside the cell to depolymerize plant cell-wall polysaccharides. Its catalytic core hydrolyzes β-linked glycans with cellulase-like chemistry and contributes to breakdown of hemicellulose, particularly xylan, thereby loosening host barriers and releasing soluble sugars that feed fungal metabolism and support colonization at the plant–fungus interface.

A secreted dicopper oxidase that catalyzes monophenolase/diphenolase reactions to generate o-quinones and melanin precursors outside the cell. By producing reactive aromatic intermediates, it drives extracellular pigment and cross-link formation that strengthens and remodels the fungal surface. The enzyme is delivered to the extracellular milieu via a vacuolar route, and its oxidative chemistry likely coordinates with lipid and fatty acid pathways that operate alongside quinone-driven matrix assembly during infection.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator in the plant-pathogenic fungus Verticillium dahliae that uses a TALE-class homeodomain and a C2H2 zinc-finger array to assemble multiprotein complexes on target promoters. By organizing co-regulator assemblies, it modulates gene programs that include sphingolipid biosynthesis, thereby coupling membrane biogenesis and stress-adaptive pathways to virulence-associated development within the host nucleus.

A secreted fungal effector that assembles extracellular complexes via an allergen-like scaffold to bind macromolecules and organize protease activity at the host–pathogen interface. By concentrating and presenting substrates in the extracellular space and at the fungal cell and spore walls, it promotes peptide breakdown that supports nutrient acquisition and virulence during infection.

A nucleocytoplasmic signaling kinase that serves as the central MAP kinase kinase within a developmental cascade controlling shoot and floral meristem programs. By binding ATP and catalyzing phosphotransfer through a conserved kinase core, it activates downstream MAP kinases to reprogram transcriptional networks that govern meristem regulation and inflorescence formation. Its activity likely shuttles toward the nucleus to coordinate gene expression with upstream cues.

A soluble cytoplasmic monooxygenase that tailors hydrophobic diterpene intermediates en route to antifungal phytoalexins. It uses a heme-dependent catalytic core to introduce late-stage oxidative modifications that steer intermediates toward the antifungal endpoints of the pathway. Operating within a cytoplasmic metabolon alongside the upstream cyclase and short‑chain dehydrogenase/reductase, it draws electrons from soluble redox partners to execute oxygenation chemistry that completes assembly of protective secondary metabolites.

A multivalent signaling scaffold in the oomycete Verticillium dahliae that oligomerizes through an N-terminal SAM module and uses a C-terminal small GTPase-binding region to assemble membrane-proximal complexes at polarized cell ends. By concentrating receptor-driven pathways and cytoskeletal regulators at cell poles, it modulates insulin receptor–like signaling and neurite-like morphogenesis, thereby coordinating polarized growth and host-interaction programs central to filamentous development and pathogenicity.

A nuclear virulence effector from a plant-pathogenic fungus that operates as a binding-driven adaptor to remodel host gene expression. By assembling transcriptional and chromatin-regulatory complexes in the nucleus, it suppresses host defense pathways and restores cellular homeostasis. This nuclear scaffolding mechanism likely reshapes transcriptional programs that intersect with antiviral and stress-response networks, thereby enhancing pathogenic fitness.

A secreted aspartic endopeptidase that operates as a broad-spectrum protease supporting nutrient acquisition and developmental remodeling in the rice blast fungus. It is produced as a soluble zymogen and activated under acidic conditions to cleave internal peptide bonds in diverse substrates. By executing extracellular proteolysis and secretory-pathway processing, it supplies peptides and amino acids that fuel growth and pathogenicity, with activity tuned by a bilobal catalytic core that positions two aspartates to activate water for hydrolysis.

A multi-pass membrane carrier in zebrafish that uses a major facilitator architecture to shuttle small solutes across the cell surface. Its fold and coupling chemistry favor proton-linked movement of monocarboxylates and extend to amino acid fluxes at the membrane. By alternating access between sides of the bilayer, it supports exchange of organic anions and modified amino acids at the plasma membrane, coordinating metabolite balance through a secondary-active transport mechanism.

A soluble signaling scaffold and enzyme that assembles higher-order complexes through armadillo repeats and a sterile alpha motif, positioning a TIR effector core to cleave NAD+ into ADP-ribose and nicotinamide. By coupling NAD+ breakdown to transcriptional control, it dampens MYC-driven programs and coordinates innate immune pathways. The complex predominantly operates in the cytoplasm and nucleus, where it shuttles between compartments to regulate gene expression and innate signaling circuits.

A secreted extracellular glycosidase that hydrolyzes hyaluronan into shorter oligosaccharides, thereby remodeling the hyaluronan-rich matrix that shapes reproductive tract microenvironments. By softening and reorganizing this extracellular scaffold, it facilitates key steps of fertilization—loosening sperm transit paths and tuning interactions at the oocyte interface—while its bioactive, matrix-perturbing activity reflects a toxin-like role in reproductive tissues.

A nucleocytoplasmic transcriptional regulator that integrates environmental and metabolic cues through a bHLH DNA-binding head and a PAS/PAC signal-sensing core. It shuttles between cytoplasm and nucleus, assembling protein complexes that activate target gene transcription in response to xenobiotics and other organic cyclic compounds. By forming selective heterodimers and recruiting co-regulators, it drives transcriptional programs central to chemical stress responses and broader homeostatic control.

A secreted bovine lipocalin that forms a soluble β-barrel to bind and transport all-trans-retinol in the extracellular space. By homodimerizing and stabilizing hydrophobic retinoids, it buffers and delivers these ligands to cell surfaces, thereby shaping extracellular retinoid pools and indirectly tuning downstream metabolic pathways. Its soluble architecture and secretion drive a mechanism centered on high-affinity retinoid capture and controlled release outside the cell.

A soluble cytoplasmic enzyme in Bacillus subtilis that uses a calycin-like barrel to bind hydrophobic aromatic carboxylates and assemble transient protein complexes that channel these substrates into central metabolism. By buffering and handing off phenolic and monocarboxylic acid intermediates, it supports carbohydrate breakdown and stabilizes cytosolic pathways linked to glycolysis. Its mechanism centers on a deep binding pocket that organizes substrates and fosters assembly with other metabolic proteins.

A cytoplasmic serine/threonine kinase that anchors to membrane–cytoskeleton interfaces and phosphorylates microtubule-associated substrates, including tau and MAP2, to tune cytoskeletal dynamics and membrane-proximal signaling. Its catalytic core transfers phosphate from ATP to serine/threonine residues, while auxiliary adaptor and membrane-targeting modules direct activity toward cytoskeletal and trafficking hubs. By activating downstream pathways through phosphorylation, it contributes to developmental decisions such as left–right patterning and operates predominantly in the cytoplasm with transient membrane association.

A soluble lipocalin that binds retinoids and related hydrophobic isoprenoid-like ligands via a calycin β-barrel, thereby stabilizing and transporting these molecules. It operates along the secretory route and in extracellular fluids, where it buffers retinoids and likely modulates their isomerization and availability to downstream pathways. By transiently associating with endoplasmic reticulum trafficking machinery and functioning as an extracellular carrier, it supports retinoid-dependent branches of isoprenoid and diterpenoid biosynthesis and prevents off-pathway chemistry through pH- and cavity-mediated ligand handling.

A SAM-dependent arginine methyltransferase that assembles into higher-order complexes to symmetrically dimethylate arginine residues on histones and RNA-binding proteins. By generating arginine methyl marks, it organizes chromatin and ribonucleoprotein assembly pathways that drive snRNP biogenesis and mRNA processing. Its shuttling between nucleus and cytoplasm, with additional associations to cytoskeletal and Golgi-related assemblies, enables coordinated control of transcriptional termination, mitotic progression, and signaling pathways governed by p53 and G protein-coupled receptors.

A cytoplasmic scaffold that assembles and regulates the beta-catenin degradation machinery. It uses an N-terminal tankyrase-recognition module to control its own turnover and complex dynamics, a central scaffold to position kinases and adaptors, and a C-terminal polymerization module that nucleates higher-order assemblies. By docking beta-catenin and juxtaposing it with destruction factors, it enforces beta-catenin turnover and thereby restrains pathways that drive proliferation and migration. Its scaffold architecture also couples to G protein-coupled receptor pathways, coordinating Wnt and GPCR signaling through transient assemblies in the cytoplasm.

A single-pass cell-surface receptor tyrosine kinase that binds membrane-tethered ephrins through a modular extracellular head, undergoes ligand-induced clustering, and activates an intracellular kinase core followed by a polymerizing SAM tail to assemble higher-order signaling assemblies. This architecture enables robust phosphorylation cascades that regulate contact-dependent cell communication, guiding immune cell activation and proliferation and tuning inflammatory responses at the plasma membrane.

A human cytoplasmic scaffold that anchors to the microtubule network and organizes signaling assemblies. An N-terminal RING module provides ubiquitin-system competence, while tandem B-boxes and a COS element drive assembly and direct microtubule binding and organization. A central Ig-like/FNIII spacer positions a C-terminal SPRY domain that captures pathway-specific partners, enabling positive control of stress-activated MAPK signaling and contributing to tissue patterning and neural development. The architecture explains accumulation in the cytoplasm and at the microtubule cytoskeleton, where it coordinates cytoskeletal remodeling with signal transduction.

A periplasmic c-type cytochrome that serves as the electron-transfer subunit of a membrane-bound dehydrogenase system in Pantoea cypripedii. It accepts electrons from the complex that oxidizes L-lactate and L-propionate to pyruvate and acetate and relays them to the respiratory chain, thereby coupling carbon catabolism to energy-conserving electron flow. Its soluble periplasmic position and high-capacity electron shuttle domain enable rapid one-electron transfers that integrate lactate/propionate utilization with downstream oxidases.

A soluble DNA-damage sensor and assembly factor in Bacillus subtilis that uses ATP-driven conformational cycling to form homotetrameric assemblies that survey and bind distorted DNA. By coupling a dedicated oligomerization module with a central DNA-binding region and a large ATPase engine, it organizes lesion recognition and handoff within the excision pathway, operating in the cytosol as part of a soluble repair complex that recruits downstream nucleases to execute excision.

A cytoplasmic scaffold that assembles and regulates the beta-catenin destruction machinery. Its N-terminus recruits tankyrase-regulated modules, a central helical scaffold organizes transient signaling assemblies, an internal site binds beta-catenin, and a C-terminal polymerizing module concentrates additional factors into a higher-order platform. By promoting beta-catenin ubiquitination and turnover, it tunes transcriptional programs that drive cell-cycle progression and cytokinesis, operating within cytoplasmic assemblies that constitute the beta-catenin destruction complex.

A cytoplasmic adaptor that binds phosphorylated sites in cytokine signaling assemblies and recruits a cullin-based ubiquitin machinery to attenuate JAK–STAT outputs. By coupling high-affinity phosphotyrosine recognition with SOCS-box–driven effector assembly, it curtails upstream tyrosine phosphorylation of STATs, dampens receptor-driven pathways, and limits apoptosis. Transient association with miRNA pathways likely coordinates post-transcriptional repression with signal termination.

A multi-pass membrane transporter that exchanges inorganic phosphate with sugar phosphates, including glycerol-3-phosphate, through an alternating-access mechanism characteristic of the major facilitator superfamily. By shuttling organophosphate esters across internal membranes, it helps balance phosphate and carbohydrate fluxes that feed hepatic glucose production and systemic glucose homeostasis. Its most likely residence is the endoplasmic reticulum membrane, where lipid–glycerol phosphate metabolism and gluconeogenic supply lines converge, enabling coordinated transmembrane transport of phosphate and carbohydrate derivatives.

A single-pass cell-surface adhesion receptor that forms a heterodimer with alpha integrin subunits to mediate high-affinity attachment to extracellular matrix and cell–cell interfaces. Its large extracellular headpiece and EGF-like stalk transmit mechanical and conformational signals, while the short cytoplasmic tail assembles intracellular adaptor complexes that organize actin stress fibers and drive migration and differentiation. By coupling adhesion to integrin-mediated and TGF-β–linked signaling, it supports epithelial cohesion and endodermal development within the integrin complex at the plasma membrane.

A constitutively active serine/threonine kinase that forms the catalytic core of a casein kinase complex and phosphorylates acidic or primed motifs on diverse substrates. By assembling into the CK2 holoenzyme and concentrating in the nucleolus, it modulates transcriptional repression and broader signaling circuits that govern development and hormone responses.
