By concentrating assembly factors at the magnetosome surface, it stabilizes higher-order complexes that tune gene-expression circuits and post-transcriptional pathways governing magnetosome formation and maintenance.

A human multi-pass membrane protein that assembles signaling complexes at the cell surface. Its transmembrane core anchors the protein and creates binding interfaces that organize and traffic membrane-associated factors, thereby enhancing the Notch pathway. By stabilizing receptor–ligand encounters and tuning endocytic routing at the plasma membrane, it functions as a scaffold that promotes productive signaling assemblies and downstream transcriptional outputs.

A soluble peroxisomal pyrophosphatase that hydrolyzes nucleoside diphosphate–linked sugars, with a strong preference for UDP-sugars such as UDP-glucose. By coordinating divalent metal ions through its Nudix catalytic core, it cleaves pyrophosphate bonds to regulate nucleotide-sugar pools. This activity tunes metabolic and redox balance within the peroxisome, linking nucleotide-sugar turnover to pathways that respond to iron availability and oxidative stress.

A multi-pass membrane acyltransferase that installs reversible palmitate modifications on target proteins to control their membrane affinity, trafficking, and signaling competence. By catalyzing lipidation at membrane leaflets, it stabilizes receptors and transporters at the cell surface, promotes their delivery and retention in dendritic and vesicular pathways, and enhances innate immune signaling by reinforcing assembly and membrane residency of cGAMP–STING complexes. Its membrane-embedded catalytic core and extensive substrate-binding surfaces coordinate palmitoylation with endocytic and phagocytic vesicle dynamics.

A soluble stromal chaperonin in Arabidopsis chloroplasts that assembles into an ATP-driven folding machine. It binds non-native polypeptides via an apical platform, uses an equatorial ATPase core to power allosteric transitions through an intermediate hinge, and cycles between open and closed states to assist folding and prevent aggregation of stromal proteins. Its activity supports proteostasis within the chloroplast, primarily in the stroma, with transient proximity to the envelope during import and assembly.

A membrane-embedded activator subunit of the intramembrane protease assembly that governs proteolytic processing of signaling receptors and precursor proteins. By stabilizing and activating the catalytic core within the membrane, it enables regulated intramembrane cleavage events that tune pathways connected to small GTPase signaling. Its multi-pass topology anchors the complex in membranes and promotes assembly and activity of the protease machinery, thereby coupling proteolysis to broader cellular signaling circuits.

A small, soluble zinc-finger regulator that binds DNA and assembles regulatory complexes to tune gene expression programs responsive to iron availability. Its N-terminal low-complexity module supports partner recruitment and nucleocytoplasmic shuttling, while the central zinc finger anchors the protein to target loci. Predominantly cytoplasmic, it likely coordinates iron-responsive transcription by coupling metal-sensing pathways to chromatin-associated regulation.

A soluble cytosolic pyrophosphohydrolase that uses a NUDIX catalytic core to hydrolyze nucleoside diphosphate–linked substrates, including ADP-ribose and diadenosine polyphosphates, thereby tuning cytosolic nucleotide pools. By controlling these labile metabolites, it supports pathways that feed into glycoprotein biogenesis and helps maintain the capacity of N-linked glycosylation. Its soluble architecture and activity situate it in the cytoplasm, where it couples nucleotide turnover to broader cellular homeostasis.

A secreted, peripherally membrane-associated alpha-class carbonic anhydrase that rapidly interconverts carbon dioxide and bicarbonate to sculpt extracellular and perisynaptic acid–base microdomains. By positioning at the cell surface and synaptic clefts, it accelerates local proton and bicarbonate production to stabilize neuronal pH homeostasis, modulate anion fluxes, and enhance inhibitory signaling. Its zinc-dependent catalytic core and soluble architecture enable high-throughput CO2/HCO3− turnover that tunes pH-regulated pathways in neurons and at membrane interfaces.

A soluble adaptor that promotes antiviral signaling by assembling and stabilizing phosphorylation-driven complexes in infected cells. It operates through multivalent protein binding to enhance host kinase pathways and transcriptional programs that restrict viral replication. The protein shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm of infected cells, coordinating cytosolic signaling with nuclear gene-expression machinery to amplify innate antiviral responses.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator that assembles into oligomeric complexes on target promoters to control epithelial gene programs governing proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis. It uses a central DNA-recognition module to bind specific regulatory elements, a tetramerization cassette to stabilize promoter-bound assemblies, and a C-terminal interaction module to recruit cofactors and chromatin regulators. Together these features enable formation of productive transcriptional complexes that elevate expression of selected target genes in human cells.

A large, multi-pass membrane channel that senses membrane tension and converts mechanical stimuli into ion-conducting activity at the cell surface. Its extended transmembrane architecture forms a tension-gated conduit whose gating is tuned by cytoskeletal and membrane-organizing partners. By coupling membrane mechanics to ion flux and membrane remodeling, it contributes to secretory pathways and broader transmembrane transport processes at the plasma membrane.

A cytoplasmic HECT-type E3 ubiquitin ligase that uses an N-terminal membrane-targeting module and central WW-mediated substrate-recognition repeats to position and capture PY-motif–bearing targets, then employs a C-terminal catalytic center to transfer ubiquitin and assemble degradation-competent chains. By decorating substrates with polyubiquitin, it promotes their proteasomal clearance and thereby shapes pathways that regulate protein quality control and turnover.

A membrane-associated cytochrome P450 monooxygenase in human cells that hydroxylates steroids and other lipophilic substrates. It anchors to intracellular membranes while presenting a cytoplasm-facing catalytic domain that uses a heme-thiolate center and electrons from NADPH-dependent redox partners to activate oxygen and insert it into bound substrates. By initiating oxidative metabolism of xenobiotics and endogenous lipids, it contributes to detoxification pathways and cellular responses to chemical stressors such as insecticides, operating primarily at the endoplasmic reticulum–microsomal interface.

A nuclear transcriptional regulator that assembles as a higher-order complex to control gene expression programs central to epithelial lineage specification and terminal differentiation. It binds specific DNA response elements via a central recognition core, oligomerizes to stabilize promoter occupancy, and uses a C‑terminal SAM platform to recruit cofactors and chromatin machinery. Through this modular architecture it activates target transcriptional networks governing epithelial morphogenesis and survival pathways, operating predominantly in the nucleus with regulated nucleocytoplasmic dynamics.

A diaphanous-related actin assembly factor in mouse that cycles between an autoinhibited state and an active barbed-end elongation machine to remodel the actin cytoskeleton. It binds small GTPases and their regulatory partners to relieve autoinhibition, then uses a dimeric actin-assembly core to nucleate and elongate filaments while recruiting profilin–actin complexes. This dynamic remodeling supports filament severing and turnover that drive substrate-coupled cell migration and phagocytic vesicle functions. The protein operates primarily in the cytosol but is recruited to membrane-proximal and vesicular compartments where actin remodeling is required.

A soluble short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase in Agrobacterium tumefaciens that uses a Rossmann-like cofactor-binding core to reduce 2-ketoacids in vitro and likely supports pyrimidine breakdown in vivo. By binding nicotinamide cofactors and employing a conserved catalytic site, it transfers hydride to carbonyl groups, helping maintain redox balance and channel uracil-derived carbon into central metabolism. The enzyme operates in the cytosol and probably participates in transient multi-enzyme assemblies that coordinate uracil catabolism.

A nuclear chromatin- and RNA-associated regulator that uses an N-terminal chromatin-reader module and a C-terminal RNA-binding module to assemble repressive ribonucleoprotein complexes. By anchoring to nucleosomes and engaging RNA, it coordinates pathways that methylate histone H3 lysine-9 and regulate DNA methylation, thereby reinforcing heterochromatin and contributing to the silencing of endogenous retrotransposons within nuclear silencing assemblies.

A nuclear scaffold that integrates DNA-damage signaling with RNA processing in Arabidopsis. It uses a chromatin-reading module to dock onto marked nucleosomes and a large armadillo-repeat platform to assemble higher-order complexes that tune stress-responsive pathways. By organizing checkpoint and RNA-maturation assemblies, it modulates responses to genotoxic stimuli and coordinates pre-mRNA splicing within nuclear protein complexes.

A multi-pass membrane carrier that mediates high-affinity, sodium-independent exchange of neutral and essential amino acids with thermodynamic coupling to intracellular gradients. It transports leucine, phenylalanine, and methionine and can exchange intracellular amino acids for extracellular osmolytes, thereby sustaining amino acid flux and indirectly shaping hormone handling by moving thyroid hormone across cellular barriers. It resides predominantly at the cell surface and dynamically traffics through endosomes and lysosomes, where its alternating-access mechanism integrates amino acid exchange with transport at physiological barriers.

A cytosolic ribonucleoprotein that assembles into neuronal RNA–protein condensates to control the fate of target mRNAs. By using a modular reader and RNA-recognition core, it binds and regulates specific transcripts that shape synaptic protein composition, thereby tuning synaptic plasticity and learning. Its soluble assemblies in the cytoplasm coordinate localized translation programs that can also influence cell–cell fusion pathways by modulating expression of fusogenic and cytoskeletal factors.

A nuclear scaffolded chromatin reader that integrates a WD40 beta-propeller with a C‑terminal acetyl‑lysine–binding module to assemble and stabilize transcriptional regulatory complexes. By docking onto acetylated nucleosomes and recruiting co-regulators, it enhances gene activation programs and likely coordinates transcription with cell‑cycle–linked pathways. Its modular architecture positions it as a hub that organizes nuclear assemblies to promote positive regulation of gene expression.

A soluble mitochondrial non-heme iron oxygenase that uses 2-oxoglutarate and oxygen to hydroxylate amino-acid-derived betaines, thereby committing flux into the carnitine pathway. It catalyzes the oxidative conversion of trimethyllysine to gamma-butyrobetaine and can further hydroxylate gamma-butyrobetaine toward hydroxy-butyrobetaine, supplying precarnitine and supporting mitochondrial acyl-carnitine metabolism. The enzyme’s TauD-like catalytic core and N-terminal scaffold coordinate Fe(II) and 2-oxoglutarate to drive precise hydroxylation chemistry that feeds carnitine biosynthesis and utilization within mitochondria.

A cytoplasmic nucleoside kinase that uses an ATP-dependent catalytic core to phosphorylate ribonucleosides—preferentially uridine and cytidine—thereby feeding the nucleotide salvage network that sustains RNA and DNA precursor pools. Its N-terminal kinase module performs phosphoryl transfer, while a C-terminal phosphoribosyltransferase-like region likely organizes higher-order assemblies and transient partnerships that tune salvage flux. By channeling ribonucleoside substrates into monophosphate intermediates without acting on adenine or guanine, it supports balanced pyrimidine and purine ribonucleotide supply in the cytoplasm.

A membrane-embedded subunit of the human gamma-secretase assembly that is required to activate the intramembrane endopeptidase core. By promoting presenilin maturation and stabilizing the active protease, it enables cleavage of diverse membrane-associated substrates and thereby tunes downstream signaling pathways. Its multi-pass topology positions it within the complex at membrane interfaces, where it enforces assembly and catalytic readiness, indirectly dampening specific catalytic and GTPase signaling circuits including those driven by Rho.

A multi-pass plasma membrane carrier that exchanges intracellular neutral amino acids for extracellular substrates to drive sodium-independent uptake of key amino acids and certain hormones. It imports leucine and phenylalanine while exporting intracellular neutral amino acids via an alternating-access mechanism, and it can also translocate thyroid hormones. By assembling into a membrane complex at the cell surface, it supports amino acid and hormone transport pathways that balance nutrient supply and signaling.

A soluble FAD-dependent proline-oxidizing enzyme in Deinococcus radiodurans that converts proline to pyrroline-2-carboxylate and donates the resulting electrons to quinone acceptors, thereby initiating proline catabolism and feeding respiratory redox flow. Its fold and chemistry indicate tight FAD binding and a cytosolic catalytic core that transiently couples to envelope-associated electron transport, functionally linking soluble amino acid breakdown to energy metabolism near the robust bacterial cell wall.

A soluble NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase/reductase in Arabidopsis that uses a short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase core to oxidize hydroxyl-bearing terpenoid intermediates to their corresponding ketones. By supplying a key redox step that generates ketone intermediates, it contributes to gibberellin biosynthesis within the cytoplasm. The enzyme binds NAD+ through a Rossmann-like fold and likely operates within a transient cytosolic metabolon that channels hydrophobic pathway intermediates toward active hormone production.

A nuclear lysine-specific histone demethylase in Arabidopsis that uses a JmjC catalytic core to remove methyl groups from histone lysines, prominently at H3K9 and also at H3K36 and H4K20. By erasing these chromatin marks, it shifts epigenetic states toward transcriptional activation, coordinating with cytosine methylation pathways and shaping gene expression programs that drive developmental decisions such as stomatal lineage progression. Its mechanism relies on Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent oxidative demethylation within a larger demethylase scaffold that targets nucleosomes in the nucleus.

A serine/threonine kinase that orchestrates polarized cell architecture by phosphorylating cytoskeletal regulators and microtubule-associated proteins. Its catalytic core drives autophosphorylation and substrate phosphorylation, while a ubiquitin-associated module recruits ubiquitin pathway components and a C-terminal KA1 element targets the enzyme to the cortex and cytoskeleton. By assembling with myosin II complexes and ubiquitin ligases at cortical sites, it establishes cell polarity and axis specification, and it promotes neuronal morphogenesis and dendritic patterning through tightly coupled phosphorylation–ubiquitin signaling.

A nuclear assembly factor that integrates into the SAGA coactivator pathway and contributes to RNA polymerase II transcription. Its histone-fold core organizes multivalent protein–protein interfaces that stabilize TAF- and TBP-associated modules, thereby promoting preinitiation complex formation and enhancing transcriptional output. By scaffolding SAGA and related assemblies in the nucleus, it supports chromatin-engaged initiation events and positively regulates DNA-templated transcription.

A multidomain nuclear scaffold and mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase that assembles and regulates genome-maintenance machines. It uses an N-terminal phospho-recognition module to dock onto DNA-damage assemblies, a WGR-like nucleic-acid–binding region and a PARP regulatory–catalytic core to engage and modify substrates, and a VIT–vWA–MVP-ID tail to stabilize higher-order complexes at chromatin and the mitotic spindle. Through these coordinated modules, it binds DNA, tunes ADP-ribosylation-dependent assemblies, and modulates pathways that govern DNA repair, telomere control, cell death, and inflammatory signaling within the nucleus and spindle-associated compartments.

A soluble human scaffold that assembles higher-order protein complexes to tune muscle contractility. Its tandem Far11/STRP modules create multivalent interfaces that organize nuclear ribonucleoprotein and chromatin-associated assemblies, thereby shaping myogenic gene expression and RNA processing. By coordinating nuclear programs that determine the availability and tuning of contractility determinants, it exerts an indirect but pivotal influence on the regulation of muscle contraction and resides predominantly in the nucleus.

A cytoplasmic actin-assembly regulator that uses an N-terminal WAVE-family scaffold and a C-terminal WH2 actin-binding module to coordinate branched filament formation at the cell periphery. By assembling and positioning actin-regulatory complexes, it promotes lamellipodial actin dynamics while suppressing excessive stress-fiber assembly. Its soluble pool concentrates at leading edges and transiently associates with Golgi-linked membranes, where it tunes actin remodeling through multivalent protein interactions rather than enzymatic catalysis.

A human LRR-based scaffold that assembles signaling and phosphatase modules to tune small GTPase pathways. Its extended leucine-rich repeat solenoid creates a high-affinity platform that stabilizes GDP-bound small GTPases and coordinates their controlled activation cycles, thereby enhancing Ras-driven signaling flux. By recruiting serine/threonine phosphatase assemblies, it couples nucleotide-state control of GTPases with reversible phosphorylation, operating as a non-enzymatic organizer that modulates pathway amplitude and timing.

A developmental scaffold that assembles signaling and chromatin-regulatory complexes to drive photoreceptor differentiation and compound eye formation in fruit fly. Its helical repeat region builds multivalent interfaces that recruit partners, while a SMYD-centered module organizes chromatin-modifying assemblies. By coupling membrane-proximal signaling to gene-expression control, it modulates transcriptional programs that specify photoreceptor identity and tissue morphogenesis, with transient association to membrane-associated hubs guiding its activity.

A cytoplasmic HECT-type ubiquitin ligase that uses an N-terminal membrane-targeting module and a central array of WW repeats to recruit and position substrates, then employs a C-terminal catalytic center to transfer ubiquitin and assemble degradation-linked polyubiquitin chains. By coupling membrane-proximal substrate capture with catalytic ubiquitin transfer, it promotes cytoplasmic proteostasis and turnover of targeted proteins.

A nuclear regulatory adaptor that binds single-stranded nucleic-acid regulatory elements and assembles transcriptional control complexes. By combining a sequence-specific single-strand recognition module with an oligomerization and scaffolding motif, it organizes protein assemblies that modulate promoter and enhancer function, thereby tuning gene expression programs within the nucleus.

A single-pass cell-surface receptor–like protein in fruit fly that presents a large extracellular ectodomain to capture external cues and assemble homodimers that initiate intracellular signaling. Its modular ligand-binding and cysteine-rich core promote clustering at the plasma membrane, where receptor assembly triggers adaptor recruitment and downstream pathways. By organizing homotypic complexes at the cell surface, it functions as a signal-transducing scaffold that converts extracellular information into intracellular responses.

A soluble enzyme in fruit fly that catalyzes the dehydration step converting GDP-mannose to GDP-fucose, thereby supplying the activated fucose pool used for diverse cellular glycosylation pathways. It operates through a NAD-dependent oxidoreductive lyase mechanism and likely functions within cytosolic biosynthetic assemblies that coordinate nucleotide-sugar production and channel GDP-fucose toward downstream glycosylation reactions.

A soluble metalloaminopeptidase that assembles into a homomultimeric complex and trims N-terminal residues from cytosolic and organelle-associated substrates. By tuning peptide and protein turnover, it supports neuronal proteostasis pathways that shape assembly and maturation of higher-order brain circuits. Its oligomeric assembly and recruitment to membrane-bounded compartments position it to modulate intracellular proteolysis during development of the central complex and mushroom body.

A small soluble factor in fruit fly that assembles cytoplasmic nucleoprotein complexes to coordinate iron-responsive pathways. Its SERF-like core and zinc finger–related scaffold enable DNA engagement and extensive RNA-associated interactions, positioning the protein primarily in the cytoplasm where it likely modulates mRNA handling and translational control during shifts in iron availability. By coupling nucleic acid–binding scaffolding with transient chromatin contacts, it helps tune gene expression and post-transcriptional programs that implement the cellular response to iron.

A small cytoplasmic nucleic-acid–binding scaffold in fruit fly that uses an EDRK-rich SERF-like core to assemble and remodel nucleoprotein complexes. By engaging DNA and RNA-associated assemblies, it likely tunes gene-expression and RNA-processing pathways that implement the cellular response to iron. Its soluble architecture supports roles in cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein hubs and iron-responsive regulatory circuits that recalibrate iron uptake, storage, and utilization.

A single-pass type II membrane glycosyltransferase in the medial Golgi of fruit fly that installs terminal α1,6-linked fucose onto secretory pathway glycans. Its luminal catalytic core transfers fucose from GDP-fucose to maturing glycoproteins, completing core-fucosylation and shaping downstream glycan elaboration that influences extracellular matrix and cell wall polysaccharide pathways. A C-terminal SH3-like module stabilizes the luminal catalytic platform and organizes interactions with Golgi-resident partners to coordinate glycosylation within the medial cisterna.

A Golgi-resident, single-pass type II membrane glycosyltransferase that installs terminal fucose via an alpha-1,3 linkage onto maturing glycoconjugates. Its luminal catalytic ectodomain uses a GT10 fold to bind GDP-fucose and acceptor glycans, producing fucosylated epitopes that tune glycoprotein function. By executing this late-stage modification in the Golgi stack, it contributes to glycan maturation and broader fucosylation pathways that shape cell-surface and secretory glycan structures.

A DAG-activated serine/threonine kinase that cycles between cytosol and peripheral membrane via tandem lipid-sensing modules. Upon diacylglycerol engagement, it relocates to membrane-proximal signaling hubs, where its catalytic core phosphorylates targets that coordinate vesicle trafficking, cytoskeletal remodeling, and stress-responsive pathways. Through scaffolded assemblies and coupling to MAPK and NF-κB axes, it modulates nuclear transport programs and cell survival decisions, integrating receptor-driven signals with cytoplasmic and membrane-localized control.

A multi-pass plasma membrane transporter that mediates high-affinity, sodium-independent exchange of amino acids. It operates bidirectionally through an alternating-access mechanism to import and export neutral and aromatic amino acids, thereby shaping intracellular pools of key substrates such as leucine and glycine. By assembling into membrane complexes at the cell surface, it coordinates amino acid flux with broader metabolic and hormonal pathways, using a central binding cavity characteristic of amino acid transporters to achieve broad substrate specificity and occasional engagement with peptide-like ligands.

A soluble human adaptor that combines a low-complexity, EDRK-rich interaction platform with a C2H2 zinc finger to bind nucleic acids and assemble regulatory complexes. By coupling scaffolded partner recruitment to direct DNA engagement, it likely coordinates transcriptional and RNA-processing pathways that adapt cells to iron availability. Its soluble architecture supports a predominant cytoplasmic role, where it organizes assemblies that relay iron-dependent signals to gene-expression machinery.

A copper/zinc-dependent superoxide dismutase that catalyzes the dismutation of superoxide into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide, thereby protecting the cell against oxidative stress. Its β-barrel fold coordinates catalytic copper and structural zinc to drive rapid radical detoxification and couple antioxidant defense to copper handling. The enzyme likely operates in the extracellular milieu, where it mitigates oxidative challenges associated with environmental and host-derived radicals, integrating with copper-trafficking pathways to sustain detoxification and stress adaptation.

An extracellular, membrane-associated regulator that assembles a pericellular scaffold to restrain matrix-remodeling proteases and dampen cell motility. Its cysteine-rich, adhesive architecture binds extracellular partners and receptors, while an inhibitory module suppresses metalloproteinase-driven proteolysis. By stabilizing the pericellular matrix and tuning receptor cues at the cell surface, it curbs migration and supports tumor-suppressive control of protease activity and tissue integrity.

A plant nodulin-related scaffold that assembles regulatory complexes to enhance gene expression. It likely associates with membranes to sense or relay signals and then engages nuclear transcriptional machinery to boost transcriptional output. By using multivalent protein-binding interfaces, it organizes transcription factors and co-activators, operating at the membrane–nucleus interface to couple upstream cues to transcriptional activation.

A soluble auxin-responsive regulatory protein that uses a SAUR-family core to assemble and modulate signaling complexes controlling early plant growth programs. By engaging partners through multivalent binding rather than catalysis, it tunes pathways that drive auxin-induced changes in cell expansion and seedling development. Its activity likely operates within soluble compartments, including a nuclear pool that coordinates transcriptional and chromatin-linked control of developmental outputs.

A large cytosolic hydrolase that opens cyclic amide intermediates during aromatic amino acid breakdown. It uses a tripartite oxoprolinase/hydantoinase architecture to hydrolyze an imide formed in the pathway that degrades phenylalanine, thereby committing carbon and nitrogen into downstream metabolic routes. The multi-domain assembly likely coordinates nucleophile activation and metal-assisted ring opening, functioning within a soluble cytoplasmic metabolon that channels phenylalanine-derived intermediates toward energy and biosynthetic balance.

A large cytosolic polyketide megasynthase that assembles and cyclizes aromatic intermediates en route to fumonisin B1. It initiates and elongates a polyketide chain via loading and condensation modules, uses malonyl-transfer chemistry to extend the backbone, and employs a product-template system to impose ring closures and aromatization. A carrier segment shuttles intermediates, and a terminal hydrolytic/cyclization module resolves the final product. By operating as a homomerizing assembly line, it channels pathway flux within the fumonisin route that culminates in B1 formation.

A soluble serine-dependent esterase in Pestalotiopsis fici that uses an alpha/beta-hydrolase catalytic core to hydrolyze carboxylic ester intermediates during assembly of anthracycline antibiotics. By editing acylated intermediates within cytoplasmic biosynthetic assemblies, it supports the formation of daunorubicin and doxorubicin and thereby contributes to broader antibiotic metabolic pathways. Its mechanism relies on a catalytic serine–histidine–aspartate triad that forms and resolves an acyl-enzyme intermediate to control the timing and fidelity of anthracycline tailoring steps.
